metadata.title: TLCTC CWE Mapping
metadata.description: Maps MITRE CWE weaknesses to TLCTC threat clusters with rationale, verdict confidence, and CVE references.
audit_history: 2026-05-06: Step 9 rationale standardization sweep — 283 stub rationales rewritten with decision-tree-citing prose. Family patterns: sanitization-of-special-elements series (CWE-140-165), server-side info-leak via artifact (CWE-526-550), hardware/SoC flaws (CWE-1190-1334) split into design / debug / side-channel / fault-injection / data-remanence / protection sub-families, resource-exhaustion (CWE-400-410, 770-779, 1325) citing Q5, malware (CWE-507-512) citing Q6 + Axiom III, deprecated entries (CWE-71/92/132/...) citing Prohibited-verdict policy, XSS variants (CWE-82-87) citing CWE-79 parent. After this sweep, 0 entries with rationales under 60 characters remain.

2026-05-05: v2.1 audit — Unreviewed bucket cleared; R-EXEC sweep (15 entries gained → #7); enabling-condition CWEs reclassified to the cluster they enable; #1 cluster fully audited (169 entries): crypto/PRNG re-clustered to #4/#5 per ruling-2 (incl. late-found CWE-1241), code-typo CWEs (CWE-481/482/483/484/486 — incl. Apple goto-fail) and comparison-bug CWEs (CWE-595/597) re-clustered to #2|#3 since they are code implementation flaws (Q2) not logic-abuse (Q9), CWE-757 algorithm-downgrade re-clustered to #5, CWE-1256 SW-HW interface re-clustered to #1|#8; ~130 stub rationales rewritten to cite the abused function and the decision-tree question. #2|#3 cluster audited (228 entries): CWE-318 cleartext-secret-in-executable re-clustered to #4 per ruling-2 (missed in Step 3 because mapping was non-N/A); CWE-21 path-traversal parent demoted to Discouraged; CWE-1066/1097 promoted from Prohibited→Allowed (verdict drift); CWE-1082 mapping → N/A as no real security relevance; ~185 stub rationales (path-traversal CWE-22..58, memory-safety CWE-119..127/131/415..476, sanitization-filtering CWE-790..796, concurrency CWE-362..821, arithmetic CWE-128/191/681) rewritten with R-ROLE-citing prose. Single-cluster spot-check audit (#2/#4/#5/#6/#9/#10): 40 #2-entries re-clustered to #2|#3 where the same flaw applies in either role per R-ROLE (memory-safety CWE-188/241/242/244/588/676/733/762/763/826/843, type-confusion CWE-843 incl. browser JIT, side-channel CWE-204..208, numeric CWE-192/194..198/839, function-call CWE-683/685..688, parser/struct CWE-237..240/253/626, concurrency CWE-663/765/768/828/831/832); CWE-300/311 verdicts Discouraged → Allowed (mappings well-defended, not abstract); CWE-1101 verdict Prohibited → Allowed; CWE-443/769 deprecated entries with non-N/A mappings fixed to N/A for consistency; CWE-1060/1072/1073/1094 performance-only Prohibited+#6 entries reclassified to Discouraged + N/A. ~30 stub rationales rewritten in #4 (credential CWEs CWE-258/259/262/263/307/308/309/321/521/613/1392/1394) and #9 (UI-deception CWE-356/357/446/451) and #10 (supply-chain CWE-510/511/553/1104/1273/1291/1297/1328) clusters. Allowed-with-Review queue narrowed from 90 to 16 intentional remainders; N/A bucket reconciled (verdict drift fixed): 62 'N/A + Allowed' entries (code-quality/consequence/non-threat) reclassified to Discouraged, and 47 'N/A + Prohibited' code-quality entries (CWE-1041–1124 'Bad Coding Practices' cluster) reclassified to Discouraged since they are concrete weakness patterns, not Category/View/Deprecated nodes. Two policy rulings codified: (1) CWE-287-style authentication-logic bypass = #1, credential application is the only #4 case; (2) enabling-condition CWEs map to the cluster they enable. Verdict semantics tightened: Prohibited now reserved exclusively for Category/View/List/Deprecated org nodes (44 entries); code-quality patterns and abstract umbrella CWEs are Discouraged (171 entries). Final state: 756 Allowed / 16 Allowed-with-Review (intentional context-dependence) / 171 Discouraged / 44 Prohibited.

notation.arrow: A → B means A enables or leads to B (attack sequence)
notation.pipe: A | B means either A or B depending on context
notation.na: N/A means the weakness is not directly mappable to a single cluster

verdict_definitions.Allowed: High-confidence mapping; CWE is specific enough for unambiguous classification
verdict_definitions.Allowed-with-Review: Mapping is reasonable but the cluster genuinely depends on a use-context that varies between concrete CVE instances; review at instance level
verdict_definitions.Discouraged: CWE is too abstract or generic for reliable mapping; classify at the more specific child CWE
verdict_definitions.Prohibited: CWE is a category/view/list/deprecated entry; not a concrete weakness

mappings.cweName: Unmapped or Unknown Weakness
mappings.mappingRationale: Placeholder identifier, not a concrete weakness. Cannot be mapped to any TLCTC cluster.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Misconfiguration: Data Transmission Without Encryption
mappings.mappingRationale: Failure to encrypt data in transit implies the vulnerability of the communication path, enabling Man in the Middle (#5).

mappings.cweName: J2EE Misconfiguration: Insufficient Session-ID Length
mappings.mappingRationale: Weak session identifiers facilitate session hijacking, which is a direct form of Identity Theft (#4).

mappings.cweName: J2EE Misconfiguration: Missing Custom Error Page
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of the legitimate error reporting function (#1) to gather reconnaissance data (Data Risk Event).

mappings.cweName: J2EE Misconfiguration: Entity Bean Declared Remote
mappings.mappingRationale: Exposing internal logic as remote interfaces allows attackers to abuse these functions (#1) beyond their intended local scope.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Misconfiguration: Weak Access Permissions for EJB Methods
mappings.mappingRationale: Overly permissive configuration allows attackers to abuse legitimate business logic functions (#1) without proper authorization.

mappings.cweName: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Creating Debug Binary
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of the legitimate debug functionality (#1) to glean system information.

mappings.cweName: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Missing Custom Error Page
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of default error handling (#1) to disclose stack traces and configuration details.

mappings.cweName: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Password in Configuration File
mappings.mappingRationale: Insecure password storage exposes credentials whose downstream use is impersonation. Decision tree Q3 (credential weakness) → #4. Note: the acquisition step takes its cluster from the access vector (per R-CRED), but the CWE itself classifies by the credential-application threat it enables.

mappings.cweName: Compiler Removal of Code to Clear Buffers
mappings.mappingRationale: Compiler removes a memset/explicit-buffer-clear because it considers the buffer dead after the clear, leaving sensitive data in memory. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
mappings.mappingRationale: The attacker manipulates inputs to abuse the system's configuration functionality (#1), altering behavior within designed (but unsafe) parameters.

mappings.cweName: Improper Input Validation
mappings.mappingRationale: Too generic to map. Input validation failures are the root cause for #2 (Injection), #3 (Client-side XSS), #6 (DoS), and #1 (Logic abuse).

mappings.cweName: Pathname Traversal and Equivalence Errors
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for path-traversal and path-equivalence errors. Specific cases classify at child CWEs (CWE-22 onward). Decision tree Q2 -> #2 | #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')

mappings.cweName: Failure to Sanitize Special Elements into a Different Plane (Special Element Injection)
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for injection flaws — failure to sanitize special elements into a different plane (data plane vs. code plane). Specific cases at child CWEs (CWE-77, 78, 79, 89, 94). Decision tree Q2 -> #2|#3 per R-ROLE; if execution chain is reached, R-EXEC adds → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Equivalent Special Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw in sanitization logic. Maps to #2 or #3.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side sanitization flaw allowing attacker data to be interpreted as commands (#2). Per R-EXEC, command execution moves the attacker's foreign code into the target's execution context — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side sanitization flaw causing data→code transition into the OS shell (#2). Per R-EXEC, OS command execution executes attacker-controlled foreign code — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client
mappings.mappingRationale: Reflected/Stored XSS exploits a server-side coding flaw (#2) to deliver a script that the browser executes (#7). DOM-based XSS exploits a client-side coding flaw (#3).

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client
mappings.mappingRationale: XSS variant. #2->#7 if server-side injection, #3 if client-side DOM.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Script in an Error Message Web Page
mappings.mappingRationale: Reflected XSS via error page. Server flaw (#2) delivers script (#7).

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes of IMG Tags in a Web Page
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client
mappings.mappingRationale: XSS variant — script payload in IMG attribute (e.g., onerror). Mapping inherited from CWE-79 parent: server-role injection delivering script for browser execution (#2 -> #7) or client-role DOM manipulation (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes in a Web Page
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client
mappings.mappingRationale: XSS variant — script in arbitrary tag attributes (onclick, onmouseover, etc.). Mapping inherited from CWE-79 parent: server-role injection delivering script for browser execution (#2 -> #7) or client-role DOM manipulation (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: The attacker manipulates arguments to abuse the logic of the called command (#1) without necessarily executing arbitrary new code (though it often leads to #7).

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side coding flaw allowing data->code transition in DB query (SQL is code). Explicitly #2 in Whitepaper.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side LDAP query construction with attacker-controlled input — LDAP injection (sibling of CWE-89 SQLi). Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: XML Injection (aka Blind XPath Injection)
mappings.mappingRationale: XML/XPath injection — implementation flaw where attacker input modifies the structure of an XML document or XPath expression interpreted server- or client-side. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Improper Sanitization of Custom Special Characters
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-138 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements) and children.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: CRLF injection — unsanitized newline in output enables HTTP response splitting (server #2) or log injection (client/server #3). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client -> Malware
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw enabling direct data→code transition (unsafe code generation/evaluation). Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE. Per R-EXEC, code injection definitionally executes foreign code — append → #7 in both branches.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client -> Malware
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw passing untrusted input to a code-evaluation primitive (eval/exec). Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE. Per R-EXEC, eval of attacker-controlled input executes foreign code — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Statically Saved Code ('Static Code Injection')
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client -> Malware
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw where attacker data is persisted into an interpreted code file (e.g., .php, .jsp). Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE. Per R-EXEC, the persisted code executes when the file is later loaded — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Server-Side Includes (SSI) Within a Web Page
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side sanitization flaw allowing attacker input to be evaluated as SSI directives. Per R-EXEC, SSI directives execute arbitrary commands on the server — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program ('PHP Remote File Inclusion')
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side implementation flaw passing attacker-controlled paths to include/require, which loads and executes the referenced PHP. Per R-EXEC, RFI is foreign code execution by definition — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of logic (#1) by manipulating IDs to access unintended resources (IDOR/Logic abuse).

mappings.cweName: Struts: Duplicate Validation Forms
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw in server-side framework configuration leading to potential logic bypass.

mappings.cweName: Struts: Incomplete validate() Method Definition
mappings.mappingRationale: Struts validate() method incomplete — server-side validation logic does not cover all fields. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role validation flaw).

mappings.cweName: Struts: Form Bean Does Not Extend Validation Class
mappings.mappingRationale: Struts form bean does not extend the validation framework class — validation never runs on its inputs. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Struts: Form Field Without Validator
mappings.mappingRationale: Struts form field has no validator declared — server-side validation is silently skipped for that field. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Struts: Plug-in Framework not in Use
mappings.mappingRationale: Configuration/best-practice issue (Struts plug-in framework not in use). No specific threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: Struts: Unused Validation Form
mappings.mappingRationale: Dead validation form — code-quality observation, not a threat action.

mappings.cweName: Struts: Unvalidated Action Form
mappings.mappingRationale: Struts ActionForm not validated — server-side request inputs reach business logic without sanitization. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Struts: Validator Turned Off
mappings.mappingRationale: Struts validation framework explicitly disabled in configuration — server-side input checks bypassed by design. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Struts: Validator Without Form Field
mappings.mappingRationale: Configuration mismatch (Struts validator without form field) — non-threat best-practice issue.

mappings.cweName: Direct Use of Unsafe JNI
mappings.mappingRationale: Direct use of unsafe JNI calls — Java code invokes native libraries that bypass the JVM's memory-safety guarantees, opening the door to native-code memory corruption. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Missing XML Validation
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing XML schema/DTD validation — implementation flaw in the parser-consumer handoff. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting')
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw. While the flaw is on the server (#2), the consequence is often Client-side XSS or Cache Poisoning (#3).

mappings.cweName: Process Control
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of library loading/process execution (#1) to execute malicious code (#7).

mappings.cweName: Misinterpretation of Input
mappings.mappingRationale: Misinterpretation of input — same input parsed differently in different contexts (similar to CWE-436 interpretation conflict). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for output-encoding flaws (XSS, log injection, command injection downstream of unencoded output). Specific cases classify at child CWEs. Per R-EXEC, where the flaw enables execution append → #7 (e.g., CWE-79, CWE-77).

mappings.cweName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side log injection — unsanitized newline/control characters in log output let an attacker forge log entries or inject terminal-escape sequences for log-viewer exploitation. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Access of Indexable Resource ('Range Error')
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for indexable-resource access errors (out-of-bounds read/write/index). Specific cases at child CWEs (CWE-119, 125, 787, 129). Memory-safety code flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for buffer-bounds violations. Specific cases classify at child CWEs (CWE-120, 121, 122, 124-127). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow')
mappings.mappingRationale: Classic stack/heap buffer overflow from missing size checks. Decision tree Q2 (code implementation flaw) - server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
mappings.mappingRationale: Stack-based buffer overflow — write past the end of a stack buffer overwrites adjacent stack frames (return address, saved registers). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
mappings.mappingRationale: Heap-based buffer overflow — write past the end of a heap allocation corrupts adjacent allocator metadata or neighboring objects. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Write-what-where Condition
mappings.mappingRationale: Write-what-where primitive — attacker controls both the value and the destination of a write. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Buffer Underwrite ('Buffer Underflow')
mappings.mappingRationale: Buffer underwrite — write to memory before the start of an allocation. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Out-of-bounds Read
mappings.mappingRationale: Out-of-bounds read — reads memory past allocation boundary, often leaking adjacent secrets (cf. Heartbleed). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Buffer Over-read
mappings.mappingRationale: Buffer over-read — reads past the end of an allocation. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Buffer Under-read
mappings.mappingRationale: Buffer under-read — reads memory before the start of an allocation. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Wrap-around Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Array Index
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper validation of array index — out-of-bounds access via attacker-controlled index. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency
mappings.mappingRationale: Length-parameter inconsistency — declared length disagrees with actual buffer size, driving over-read or over-write. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size
mappings.mappingRationale: Buffer-size calculation error (off-by-one, integer overflow in size math) leads to under-allocated buffers. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Miscalculated Null Termination
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into broader buffer-handling CWEs (CWE-119 family).

mappings.cweName: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
mappings.mappingRationale: Format-string vulnerability — attacker-controlled format string is passed to printf-family, enabling memory read/write via %n and friends. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Calculation of Multi-Byte String Length
mappings.mappingRationale: Multi-byte string length miscalculation (UTF-8 byte count vs. code-point count) leads to incorrect buffer sizing. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side sanitization-failure variant — failure to neutralize multiple internal special elements in input that flows into a downstream interpreter (shell, SQL, log, query, parser). Decision tree Q2 -> #2. See CWE-138 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements) parent for the umbrella discussion.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Missing Special Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side parser flaw — missing required special element (e.g., absent close-tag, missing terminator) puts the parser in unintended state. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Additional Special Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side parser flaw — additional/unexpected special element parsed where none was expected. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Inconsistent Special Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side parser flaw — inconsistent special elements (mismatched delimiters, conflicting markers). Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Null Termination
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper null-termination of C strings — string operations read or write past intended boundary. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Encoding Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Encoding-handling bugs (charset confusion, UTF-7/UTF-8 normalization) cause sanitizer/parser bypass. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Alternate Encoding
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side parser flaw — alternate input encoding (UTF-7, IDN, percent-encoded) bypasses sanitization that operated on the canonical form. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Double Decoding of the Same Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Double-decoding bug — input decoded twice (e.g., URL-decoded then HTML-decoded) reintroduces special characters that were neutralized in the first pass. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Mixed Encoding
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side parser flaw — mixed encodings in a single input stream (UTF-8 + Windows-1252 fragments) cause sanitizer/consumer to interpret bytes differently. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Unicode Encoding
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper Unicode handling — surrogate pairs, normalization forms, or homoglyphs bypass sanitizers that operated on a different normalization. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of URL Encoding (Hex Encoding)
mappings.mappingRationale: URL/percent-encoding handling flaw — case variation, double-encoding, or partial decoding lets attacker payloads slip past validators. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity
mappings.mappingRationale: Case-sensitivity handling mismatch between security check and downstream consumer (e.g., 'ADMIN' vs. 'admin') lets an attacker bypass the check via casing variation. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Behavior Order: Early Validation
mappings.mappingRationale: Validation runs at the wrong stage of input processing (e.g., before canonicalization), so post-canonicalization the value is no longer what was validated. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role validation logic flaw).

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize
mappings.mappingRationale: Validation precedes canonicalization — validator sees the raw form while the consumer sees the canonical form. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Filter
mappings.mappingRationale: Validation precedes filtering — filter modifies the value after validation already approved it. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Collapse of Data into Unsafe Value
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization step collapses multi-character sequences into a single character, allowing inputs that pass validation to expand into payloads downstream. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Permissive List of Allowed Inputs
mappings.mappingRationale: Allowlist that admits unsafe inputs becomes the validation flaw enabling injection-style exploits in server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) code per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs
mappings.mappingRationale: Incomplete denylist leaves residual unsafe inputs that drive injection/exploit attempts in server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) code per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Regular Expression
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw. Regular expressions are used heavily in both Server (#2) and Client (#3) logic.

mappings.cweName: Overly Restrictive Regular Expression
mappings.mappingRationale: Overly restrictive regex usually causes false rejects (availability/UX), not a security threat. Per Axiom III not a generic vulnerability cause.

mappings.cweName: Partial String Comparison
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication/authorization check that compares only a prefix or partial string lets an attacker submit a value matching the prefix. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the comparison function's logic).

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Data/Memory Layout
mappings.mappingRationale: Reliance on data/memory layout (struct alignment, register packing) — when assumptions break, memory corruption follows. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound)
mappings.mappingRationale: Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Integer Coercion Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Integer-coercion error (implicit conversion changes value across types). Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Off-by-one Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Off-by-one in loop bounds, buffer sizing, or index arithmetic. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unexpected Sign Extension
mappings.mappingRationale: Unexpected sign extension (signed-to-larger-unsigned promotion sign-extends, producing a huge positive). Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Signed to Unsigned Conversion Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Signed-to-unsigned conversion error — negative becomes a very large positive, often used as size. Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unsigned to Signed Conversion Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Unsigned-to-signed conversion error — large positive becomes negative, breaking sign-dependent logic. Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Numeric Truncation Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Numeric truncation error (assigning into a smaller integer type drops the high bits). Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Incorrect Byte Ordering
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of incorrect byte ordering (host vs. network endianness mishandled) yields wrong values in protocol/file parsing. Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive information inserted into sent data (response body, telemetry, error reply). Implementation flaw in the data-emission function. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Data Queries
mappings.mappingRationale: Aggregated/inferential queries reveal sensitive data the user is not authorized to view directly. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the query function via inference).

mappings.cweName: Observable Discrepancy
mappings.mappingRationale: Observable discrepancy (timing, error-message difference, behavior change) leaks information through side channel. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Observable Response Discrepancy
mappings.mappingRationale: Observable side-channel discrepancy — code implementation flaw that leaks information through a measurable difference. Server-role (#2, e.g., timing-attack on auth) or client-role (#3, e.g., cache-timing in browser) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Observable Behavioral Discrepancy
mappings.mappingRationale: Observable side-channel discrepancy — code implementation flaw that leaks information through a measurable difference. Server-role (#2, e.g., timing-attack on auth) or client-role (#3, e.g., cache-timing in browser) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Observable Internal Behavioral Discrepancy
mappings.mappingRationale: Observable side-channel discrepancy — code implementation flaw that leaks information through a measurable difference. Server-role (#2, e.g., timing-attack on auth) or client-role (#3, e.g., cache-timing in browser) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Observable Behavioral Discrepancy With Equivalent Products
mappings.mappingRationale: Observable behavioral discrepancy with equivalent products — version-fingerprinting via differential responses. Server-role (#2, e.g., timing-attack on auth) or client-role (#3, e.g., cache-timing in browser) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Observable Timing Discrepancy
mappings.mappingRationale: Observable timing discrepancy (timing oracle) — used for credential brute-force, padding-oracle, side-channel decryption. Observable side-channel discrepancy — code implementation flaw that leaks information through a measurable difference. Server-role (#2, e.g., timing-attack on auth) or client-role (#3, e.g., cache-timing in browser) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Error messages emitted to the user contain sensitive internal details (stack traces, paths, query fragments). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (the error-emission function discloses more than intended).

mappings.cweName: Self-generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Self-generated error messages (logs, debug output rendered to user) include sensitive context. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the error-emission function).

mappings.cweName: Externally-Generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Externally-generated error messages (from libraries, frameworks) propagate sensitive info to the user. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the error-emission function).

mappings.cweName: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper removal of sensitive information before storage/transfer (e.g., not stripping metadata, leaving redaction reversible). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies
mappings.mappingRationale: Privacy/exposure policy is incompatible across system boundaries (e.g., internal logs surfaced via error pages, user data in URL query strings). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the policy-enforcement function).

mappings.cweName: Invocation of Process Using Visible Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Process invocation that exposes sensitive arguments via process listing (ps, /proc/*/cmdline). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Debug code left active in production exposes internal state to users. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the debug-output function in a context where it should not be reachable).

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Containment Errors (Container Errors)
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Container errors umbrella deprecated; classify at child weakness.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Failure to Protect Stored Data from Modification
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into broader integrity-protection CWEs.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Failure to provide confidentiality for stored data
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into broader confidentiality-protection CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Storage of File with Sensitive Data Under Web Root
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive files (config, backups, logs) placed under the document root are directly fetchable via HTTP. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the web server's file-serving function).

mappings.cweName: Storage of File With Sensitive Data Under FTP Root
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive files placed under the FTP root are directly fetchable. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the FTP file-serving function).

mappings.cweName: Information Loss or Omission
mappings.mappingRationale: Per Axiom III, this describes a consequence (integrity/availability impact), not a generic vulnerability. Classify by the cause that produced the loss/omission, not by the loss itself.

mappings.cweName: Truncation of Security-relevant Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Truncation of security-relevant information (logs, identifiers, hashes) drops bytes the consumer needs for correct security decisions. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Omission of Security-relevant Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Omission of security-relevant information (event fields, audit attributes) leaves downstream checks operating on incomplete data. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Obscured Security-relevant Information by Alternate Name
mappings.mappingRationale: Alternate names for security-relevant identifiers (case variation, encoding, aliases) bypass logging or access checks that match only the canonical form. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: General Information Management Problems
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. General information-management umbrella deprecated; classify at child weakness.

mappings.cweName: Sensitive Information in Resource Not Removed Before Reuse
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive information left in a resource (memory, file, buffer) before that resource is released and reused. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Syntactically Invalid Structure
mappings.mappingRationale: Parser logic flaw. Client-side parsers (e.g., XML/JSON in browsers/apps) are equally vulnerable (#3).

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of values — server-side function does not correctly process the input value (range, format, encoding). Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Missing Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of missing values — server-side function does not gracefully handle absent fields, defaulting to insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Extra Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of extra values — server-side function does not reject unexpected additional inputs (e.g., extra form fields, JSON properties). Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Undefined Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of undefined values — server-side function does not reject inputs with no valid mapping. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Parameters
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of parameters in HTTP/function calls — wrong arity or coupling between parameters. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Failure to Handle Missing Parameter
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent of missing-parameter handling flaws — child CWEs cover specific cases. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role default).

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Extra Parameters
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of extra parameters — server accepts and processes parameters beyond what was specified. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Undefined Parameters
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of undefined parameters — server processes parameters with no defined behavior, often producing undefined state. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Structural Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of structural elements (unexpected XML/JSON nesting, nested arrays). Parser logic flaw. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Incomplete Structural Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of incomplete structural elements (truncated TLV, half-closed XML). Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Failure to Handle Incomplete Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Failure to handle incomplete elements in input streams. Parser logic flaw. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Inconsistent Structural Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of inconsistent structural elements (conflicting length headers, contradictory metadata). Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Unexpected Data Type
mappings.mappingRationale: Type confusion via unexpected data type — sibling of CWE-704. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Inherently Dangerous Function
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of inherently dangerous functions (strcpy, gets, sprintf without bounds) — applicable to any C/C++ component. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Creation of chroot Jail Without Changing Working Directory
mappings.mappingRationale: chroot jail created without changing working directory — the calling process retains access to its original FS root, defeating the jail. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Clearing of Heap Memory Before Release ('Heap Inspection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Heap memory not cleared before release leaves sensitive data harvestable from later allocations. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Bad Practices: Direct Management of Connections
mappings.mappingRationale: J2EE best-practice violation (direct connection management) — stability/performance, not a threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Bad Practices: Direct Use of Sockets
mappings.mappingRationale: J2EE best-practice violation (direct socket use) — non-threat code-quality issue.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Reliance on DNS Lookups in a Security Decision
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-350 (Reliance on Reverse DNS).

mappings.cweName: Uncaught Exception
mappings.mappingRationale: Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Often Misused: Path Manipulation
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-22 (Path Traversal) family.

mappings.cweName: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges
mappings.mappingRationale: Configuration flaw allowing abuse of functions with high privilege (#1).

mappings.cweName: Unchecked Return Value
mappings.mappingRationale: Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Check of Function Return Value
mappings.mappingRationale: Incorrect check of function return value (treating partial-success as success, ignoring -1 from system calls). Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Plaintext Storage of a Password
mappings.mappingRationale: Plaintext password storage exposes credentials for downstream impersonation. Decision tree Q3 (credential weakness) → #4.

mappings.cweName: Storing Passwords in a Recoverable Format
mappings.mappingRationale: Reversible password storage (encrypted vs. one-way hashed) exposes credentials once the storage is reached. Decision tree Q3 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Empty Password in Configuration File
mappings.mappingRationale: Empty password in configuration file — trivial credential allowing impersonation. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Use of Hard-coded Password
mappings.mappingRationale: Hard-coded password baked into the product's source/binaries — once extracted, every deployment is impersonable. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Password in Configuration File
mappings.mappingRationale: Password kept in a configuration file is recoverable for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Weak Encoding for Password
mappings.mappingRationale: Trivially-reversible password encoding (Base64, ROT13) exposes credentials. Decision tree Q3 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Not Using Password Aging
mappings.mappingRationale: No password aging policy — long-lived credentials enlarge the window for offline brute force or reuse-after-leak. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Password Aging with Long Expiration
mappings.mappingRationale: Password aging interval is too long, providing only nominal rotation. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Privilege Assignment
mappings.mappingRationale: Privilege assignment grants users access to functions outside their intended role, abusable through the over-granted function. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Privilege Defined With Unsafe Actions
mappings.mappingRationale: Privilege definition includes unsafe actions (overly broad capabilities). Holders of the privilege can abuse the unsafe action to escalate. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Privilege Chaining
mappings.mappingRationale: Chained privilege grants let a holder of low privilege escalate by composing legitimately-granted capabilities. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Privilege Management
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for privilege-escalation logic flaws. Specific cases classify at child CWEs (CWE-250, 266-273, 648). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Privilege Context Switching Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Privilege context-switching error (e.g., setuid/seteuid mishandling) leaves elevated context active when it should be dropped. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Privilege Dropping / Lowering Errors
mappings.mappingRationale: Failure to drop privileges leaves later operations running with excess rights, abusable through the elevated function (#1). Decision tree Q9.

mappings.cweName: Least Privilege Violation
mappings.mappingRationale: Code runs with more privileges than required; any defect in that code is exploitable at the elevated privilege. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the over-privileged function).

mappings.cweName: Improper Check for Dropped Privileges
mappings.mappingRationale: Failure to verify privilege drop succeeded leaves elevated context active despite the attempt. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Insufficient Privileges
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for insufficient-privilege error-handling flaws. Specific cases classify at child CWEs. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Default Permissions
mappings.mappingRationale: Default permissions on created resources allow access by unintended principals. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the over-permissioned resource).

mappings.cweName: Insecure Inherited Permissions
mappings.mappingRationale: Inherited permissions are too broad, exposing resources to unintended principals. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insecure Preserved Inherited Permissions
mappings.mappingRationale: Permissions inherited from a less-trusted parent are preserved when they should be reset. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Execution-Assigned Permissions
mappings.mappingRationale: Execution-assigned permissions (setuid/setgid) are wrong, granting unintended capabilities. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Insufficient Permissions or Privileges
mappings.mappingRationale: Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Preservation of Permissions
mappings.mappingRationale: Permissions are not preserved across operations (file copy/move dropping ACLs), letting access widen. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Ownership Management
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper file/object ownership management lets an attacker abuse the ownership-dependent function (e.g., sudo bypass, file overwrite). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Unverified Ownership
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource ownership not verified before privileged action lets an attacker invoke the action on resources they do not own. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Access Control
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for access control flaws. Abuse of functions due to missing/weak checks (#1).

mappings.cweName: Improper Authorization
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for authorization flaws. Specific cases classify at child CWEs (CWE-862 missing-authz, CWE-863 incorrect-authz). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect User Management
mappings.mappingRationale: Incorrect user-management logic (orphaned accounts, role drift) lets the wrong user invoke privileged functions. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for authentication weaknesses. Per ruling-1, authentication-LOGIC bypass (skipping or fooling the check) is #1; credential-handling weaknesses (storage, generation, transmission) classify to #4 separately. Specific cases classify at child CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication can be bypassed via an alternate path/channel that does not invoke the check. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Authentication Bypass by Alternate Name
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication can be bypassed by submitting an alternate name that resolves to the same identity but is not properly checked. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication can be bypassed by spoofing identity attributes (forged tokens, replayed credentials, manipulated identity headers). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on IP Address for Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication based on source IP can be defeated by spoofing or proxying. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Trusting Self-reported DNS Name
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-350 (Reliance on Reverse DNS for security decision).

mappings.cweName: Using Referer Field for Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication based on Referer header can be defeated by setting/forging the header. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
mappings.mappingRationale: Replay attacks exploit a weakness in the authentication protocol design (#1) that fails to prevent reuse of captured authentication data. The protocol's functional logic allows replayed messages to be accepted as valid. This is abuse of the protocol's designed behavior, not exploitation of a network position. Note: If credentials are replayed to impersonate identity, the sequence is #1 â†’ #4.

mappings.cweName: Improper Certificate Validation
mappings.mappingRationale: This is a client-side code implementation flaw (#3) where certificate validation logic is improperly implemented or missing. The vulnerability exists in the client's source code that fails to correctly validate certificates. While this enables MitM scenarios, the threat being exploited is the coding bug itself.

mappings.cweName: Improper Following of a Certificate's Chain of Trust
mappings.mappingRationale: Client-side code implementation flaw (#3) in certificate chain validation logic. The developer failed to properly implement chain-of-trust verification in the client software.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch
mappings.mappingRationale: Client-side code implementation flaw (#3) where hostname verification against certificate CN/SAN is missing or incorrectly implemented. The bug is in the client's validation code.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Certificate Expiration
mappings.mappingRationale: Client-side code implementation flaw (#3) where certificate expiration check is missing or improperly implemented in the client software.

mappings.cweName: Improper Check for Certificate Revocation
mappings.mappingRationale: Client-side code implementation flaw (#3) where OCSP/CRL revocation checking is missing or improperly implemented. The vulnerability is in the client's certificate handling code.

mappings.cweName: Channel Accessible by Non-Endpoint
mappings.mappingRationale: Communication channel where the attacker is in a position between the legitimate endpoints — the canonical Man-in-the-Middle precondition. Decision tree Q4 -> #5.

mappings.cweName: Reflection Attack in an Authentication Protocol
mappings.mappingRationale: Reflection attacks exploit weaknesses in authentication protocol design (#1) where challenges can be reflected back to the challenger. The protocol's functional logic itself is vulnerable to manipulation. This is abuse of the protocol's designed behavior through parameter manipulation.

mappings.cweName: Authentication Bypass by Assumed-Immutable Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication relies on data the attacker can modify (cookie flags, hidden form fields, client-side state). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Implementation of Authentication Algorithm
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication algorithm is implemented incorrectly (skipping a step, comparing wrong values, accepting weak inputs). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Missing Critical Step in Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication flow is missing a critical step (no signature verification, no timing check), letting an attacker bypass it. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Authentication Bypass by Primary Weakness
mappings.mappingRationale: Meta-CWE: 'authentication bypass by primary weakness'. Classify the underlying primary weakness, not this wrapper.

mappings.cweName: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
mappings.mappingRationale: The attacker abuses a function (#1) that was intended to be restricted but wasn't.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
mappings.mappingRationale: No throttling/lockout on authentication attempts permits credential brute-force. Decision tree Q3 -> #4. (For non-auth endpoints, the rate-limit pattern is CWE-799 -> #4|#6.)

mappings.cweName: Use of Single-factor Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Single-factor authentication: compromise of the one factor grants full access. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Use of Password System for Primary Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Password-only primary authentication for a high-value system — passwords are the weakest factor against phishing/leak/reuse. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive data sent unencrypted in transit makes the channel exploitable for an interceptor. Per ruling-2 (enabling-condition policy) and Q4 -> #5.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Cleartext storage of sensitive data; in the dominant case the data is credentials/tokens enabling #4 Identity Theft. For non-credential PII, the impact is a confidentiality DRE rather than a distinct cluster — classify at the access-vector cluster (per R-CRED) for credential cases and at the DRE level for general PII.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Storage in a File or on Disk
mappings.mappingRationale: Cleartext on-disk storage typically exposes credentials/tokens for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 → #4 (credential case). For non-credential PII, the threat is a confidentiality DRE driven by the access-vector cluster.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Storage in the Registry
mappings.mappingRationale: Cleartext credential/token storage in the Windows registry exposes secrets for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in a Cookie
mappings.mappingRationale: Session cookies are credentials by function; cleartext cookie storage exposes them for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 → #4. The acquisition-step cluster (e.g., #3 via XSS, #5 via MitM) is separate from this CWE per R-CRED.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in Memory
mappings.mappingRationale: Cleartext credentials/tokens in memory are recoverable (via #7 Malware-driven memory read, #8 cold-boot/DMA, or debug capture) for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 → #4. Acquisition cluster is separate per R-CRED.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in Memory
mappings.mappingRationale: Memory exposure. A critical issue for Client apps (#3) where physical/local access is more likely.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in Executable
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive secrets (API keys, credentials, encryption keys) compiled into the executable are recoverable via reverse engineering. Per ruling-2 (enabling-condition CWEs map to the cluster they enable) -> #4 (the recovered credential is then applied for impersonation). Acquisition cluster (#2 / #3 / static analysis) is separate per R-CRED.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing encryption in transit makes the communication path the exploitable surface for #5 Man in the Middle (interception/eavesdropping). Decision tree Q4 (communication-path weakness) → #5; consistent with CWE-5 and CWE-311.

mappings.cweName: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
mappings.mappingRationale: Hard-coded cryptographic key in the binary — once extracted, every deployment's encrypted data and authenticated calls are reproducible by the attacker. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Key Exchange without Entity Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Key exchange without authenticating the peer endpoint — the key is established with whoever happens to be on the wire (the attacker if positioned). Decision tree Q4 -> #5.

mappings.cweName: Reusing a Nonce, Key Pair in Encryption
mappings.mappingRationale: Nonce/key reuse breaks confidentiality of authenticated-encryption modes (e.g., AES-GCM), recoverable by an interceptor. Per ruling-2 → #5.

mappings.cweName: Use of a Key Past its Expiration Date
mappings.mappingRationale: Continuing to use an expired key extends the window in which a compromised key still decrypts/authenticates traffic, exposing the channel to an interceptor. Per ruling-2 → #5.

mappings.cweName: Missing Cryptographic Step
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Man in the Middle or Identity Theft
mappings.mappingRationale: An omitted step (e.g., missing MAC, missing certificate validation, missing key derivation) collapses the protection. Channel/data cases → #5; credential-handling cases → #4. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Inadequate Encryption Strength
mappings.mappingRationale: Insufficient encryption strength makes the protected channel/data tractable for an interceptor. Per ruling-2 (enabling-condition CWEs map to the cluster they enable) and decision tree Q4 → #5.

mappings.cweName: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Man in the Middle or Identity Theft
mappings.mappingRationale: Broken/risky algorithms degrade the protection they provide. When used for transit/data encryption → #5 (recoverable plaintext for an interceptor); when used for credential hashing/MAC → #4 (recoverable credential). Per ruling-2 enabling-condition policy.

mappings.cweName: Use of Weak Hash
mappings.mappingRationale: Weak password/credential hashes are reversible by precomputation (rainbow tables) or brute force, exposing credentials for impersonation. Per ruling-2 → #4. (Non-credential hash uses fall to #5 — see CWE-327.)

mappings.cweName: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode
mappings.mappingRationale: Predictable IVs in CBC mode enable chosen-plaintext attacks against the encrypted channel/data, breaking confidentiality for an interceptor. Per ruling-2 → #5.

mappings.cweName: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Abuse of Functions or Identity Theft
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of PRNG functions (#1). If used for session/auth, leads to Identity Theft (#4).

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Entropy
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: Insufficient entropy makes generated values guessable. When the value is a session token/identifier → #4 (impersonation); when it is a key/IV → #5 (channel decryption). Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Entropy in PRNG
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: PRNG with insufficient entropy yields predictable outputs. Token/identifier use → #4; key/IV use → #5. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Insufficient Entropy in TRNG
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: Failure to detect/handle TRNG entropy starvation produces predictable outputs. Token/identifier use → #4; key/IV use → #5. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Small Space of Random Values
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: A small value space lets an attacker enumerate the full range. Token/identifier use → #4; key/IV use → #5. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Usage of Seeds in Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: Seed misuse (constant, low-entropy, exposed) makes PRNG outputs predictable. Token/identifier use → #4; key/IV use → #5. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Same Seed in Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: A reused seed produces identical PRNG sequences across runs/users, making outputs trivially predictable. Token/identifier use → #4; key/IV use → #5. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Predictable Seed in Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: Predictable seeds (e.g., time-based) let an attacker reproduce the PRNG sequence. Token/identifier use → #4; key/IV use → #5. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: Non-cryptographic PRNGs (Mersenne Twister, java.util.Random) are state-recoverable from outputs. Token/identifier use → #4; key/IV use → #5. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Small Seed Space in PRNG
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: A small seed space lets an attacker brute-force the seed and predict the entire PRNG sequence. Token/identifier use → #4; key/IV use → #5. Per ruling-2.

mappings.cweName: Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers
mappings.mappingRationale: Predictable session/token IDs let an attacker derive a valid credential and impersonate the legitimate user. Per ruling-2 → #4. (When the predictable value is a key, see CWE-327/#5.)

mappings.cweName: Predictable from Observable State
mappings.mappingRationale: Token/identifier derivable from observable state lets an attacker compute a valid credential and impersonate the legitimate user. Per ruling-2 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Predictable Exact Value from Previous Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Sequential/derivable next-value lets an attacker compute the next valid token/identifier and impersonate. Per ruling-2 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Predictable Value Range from Previous Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Constrained range from prior outputs lets an attacker brute-force the next valid token/identifier. Per ruling-2 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Use of Invariant Value in Dynamically Changing Context
mappings.mappingRationale: An invariant value is reused in a context where it should change between uses (nonces, tokens, IDs), letting an attacker exploit the predictability. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for data-authenticity verification flaws. Specific cases classify at child CWEs. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Origin Validation Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Failure to validate the origin of a request (Origin/Referer/postMessage source) lets an attacker invoke functions on behalf of an unintended caller. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Supply Chain Attack or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: Enables #10 (malicious update) or #5 (modification in transit).

mappings.cweName: Use of Less Trusted Source
mappings.mappingRationale: A security decision relies on a less-trusted source (HTTP header, client-supplied attribute) when a more-authoritative source is available. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Untrusted data is accepted alongside trusted data and treated as authoritative (e.g., signed-payload-with-extra-unsigned-fields). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Reverse DNS Resolution for a Security-Critical Action
mappings.mappingRationale: Reverse DNS lookup is used as an authoritative identity check despite being attacker-influenceable. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Type Distinction
mappings.mappingRationale: Insufficient type distinction lets attacker substitute one object type for another, causing the consumer to misinterpret content (type confusion). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
mappings.mappingRationale: CSRF forces the victim's browser to invoke a legitimate function (#1) on the server using the victim's session.

mappings.cweName: Missing Support for Integrity Check
mappings.mappingRationale: Code implementation flaw (#2/#3) where integrity checking (HMAC, signatures, checksums) was not implemented in the software. The coding omission enables tampering.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value
mappings.mappingRationale: Code implementation flaw (#2/#3) in the logic that validates integrity values (HMAC, checksums, signatures). The validation code itself contains bugs.

mappings.cweName: Product UI does not Warn User of Unsafe Actions
mappings.mappingRationale: UI does not warn the user before performing an unsafe action (overwrite, dangerous download, irreversible change). Per ruling-2, this enables user-deception attacks. Decision tree -> #9.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient UI Warning of Dangerous Operations
mappings.mappingRationale: UI warning for dangerous operations is missing or insufficient (low-contrast, easily-dismissed, after-the-fact). Per ruling-2 -> #9.

mappings.cweName: Improperly Implemented Security Check for Standard
mappings.mappingRationale: Improperly implemented security check for a published standard (TLS, OAuth, JWT). Code implementation flaw in protocol handling. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
mappings.mappingRationale: Per Axiom III a consequence (privacy/confidentiality loss), not a generic vulnerability. Classify by the cause that exposed the data.

mappings.cweName: Trust of System Event Data
mappings.mappingRationale: System event data is trusted as authoritative without verifying its origin or integrity. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
mappings.mappingRationale: Race condition (TOCTOU, concurrent state mutation) in shared-resource handling. Code implementation flaw - server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Race Condition Enabling Link Following
mappings.mappingRationale: Race condition that enables symlink-following — TOCTOU between path check and file open. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Signal Handler Race Condition
mappings.mappingRationale: Signal handler races against the main control flow, executing in undefined intermediate state. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Race Condition in Switch
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-367 (TOCTOU).

mappings.cweName: Race Condition within a Thread
mappings.mappingRationale: Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
mappings.mappingRationale: TOCTOU — security check on a property reads a value that changes before the action consuming it. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Context Switching Race Condition
mappings.mappingRationale: Context-switching race — privilege/identity context changes between check and use. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Divide By Zero
mappings.mappingRationale: Divide by zero — arithmetic exception causing process termination (DoS). Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Missing Check for Certificate Revocation after Initial Check
mappings.mappingRationale: Client-side code implementation flaw (#3) in session/connection handling where revocation status is not re-validated during long-lived sessions.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Internal State Distinction
mappings.mappingRationale: Incomplete distinction between internal program states leads to logic errors where the consumer treats different states as equivalent. Code implementation flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: State Synchronization Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into broader synchronization / state-management CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Passing Mutable Objects to an Untrusted Method
mappings.mappingRationale: Mutable object passed to untrusted method — callee can mutate caller's state. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Returning a Mutable Object to an Untrusted Caller
mappings.mappingRationale: Mutable object returned to untrusted caller — caller can mutate internal state. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Insecure Temporary File
mappings.mappingRationale: Predictable/insecure temporary-file handling enables symlink races and content substitution. Code implementation flaw - server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions
mappings.mappingRationale: Temporary file is created with permissions wider than necessary, exposing its content or letting an attacker substitute it. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions
mappings.mappingRationale: Temporary file is created in a directory whose permissions allow attackers to substitute or read the file. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Bad Practices: Use of System.exit()
mappings.mappingRationale: J2EE best-practice violation (System.exit) — stability/availability concern, not a threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Bad Practices: Direct Use of Threads
mappings.mappingRationale: J2EE best-practice violation (direct thread use) — non-threat code-quality issue.

mappings.cweName: Session Fixation
mappings.mappingRationale: Weak session management allows an attacker to fix or reuse a victim's session identifier. The attacker thereby creates/possesses a valid credential (the session ID) and uses it to impersonate the victim, which is #4 Identity Theft in TLCTC.

mappings.cweName: Covert Timing Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Covert timing channel — emanations from execution timing leak data to an observer. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / side-channel weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Symbolic Name not Mapping to Correct Object
mappings.mappingRationale: Symbolic name resolves to wrong object (e.g., DNS rebinding, symlink). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Detection of Error Condition Without Action
mappings.mappingRationale: Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unchecked Error Condition
mappings.mappingRationale: Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Missing Report of Error Condition
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing error report hampers detection but is not a threat action (per Axiom III, observability ≠ threat).

mappings.cweName: Return of Wrong Status Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unexpected Status Code or Return Value
mappings.mappingRationale: Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of NullPointerException Catch to Detect NULL Pointer Dereference
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/style issue (using NullPointerException catch for null detection). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Declaration of Catch for Generic Exception
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/style issue (catch generic Exception). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Declaration of Throws for Generic Exception
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/style issue (declare throws Exception). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for uncontrolled-resource-consumption flaws. Specific cases classify at child CWEs (CWE-770, 774, 789). Resource exhaustion / denial of service — finite capacity weakness. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — memory not released after effective lifetime — leak grows over time until OOM. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Transmission of Private Resources into a New Sphere ('Resource Leak')
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource (file handle, socket, child-process inheritance) crosses to a less-trusted sphere where it should not be reachable. Implementation flaw in resource handoff - server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of File Descriptor to Unintended Control Sphere ('File Descriptor Leak')
mappings.mappingRationale: File descriptor / handle leaked to unintended sphere (Android Binder, exec'd child process). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — resource not properly shut down or released, accumulating until exhaustion. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification)
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — asymmetric resource consumption (small request triggers large work / large allocation) — amplification primitive. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Control of Network Message Volume (Network Amplification)
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — missing rate-limit on incoming network message volume — network-flooding amplifier. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
mappings.mappingRationale: Algorithmic complexity is explicitly called out in R-FLOOD as #2/#3

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Behavior Order: Early Amplification
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — early amplification — server allocates resources before authenticating, magnifying flooding impact. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — zip-bomb / decompression-bomb — small compressed input expands to GBs. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Resource Pool
