mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — insufficient resource pool (thread pool, connection pool too small for load). Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Unrestricted Externally Accessible Lock
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — externally-accessible lock that any caller can acquire and hold, blocking the protected resource. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Improper Resource Locking
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper resource locking. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Missing Lock Check
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing lock check — code proceeds without verifying the lock was acquired. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Double Free
mappings.mappingRationale: Double free — same pointer freed twice, corrupting allocator state. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use After Free
mappings.mappingRationale: Use after free — pointer dereferenced after the underlying allocation has been freed. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unprotected Primary Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: The product's primary administrative channel is unprotected, letting any caller invoke admin functions. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Unprotected Alternate Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: An alternate channel (debug port, secondary protocol) is unprotected, letting attackers invoke functions that the primary channel would have authenticated. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Race Condition During Access to Alternate Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Race during access to an alternate channel. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unprotected Windows Messaging Channel ('Shatter')
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of intended messaging functionality (#1) to escalate privilege.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Proxied Trusted Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-300 (Channel Accessible by Non-Endpoint).

mappings.cweName: Improper Protection of Alternate Path
mappings.mappingRationale: An alternate path/channel exists that bypasses the intended authorization function. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Direct Request ('Forced Browsing')
mappings.mappingRationale: Direct request to a URL/endpoint bypasses UI-only access controls; the server must enforce, not merely the UI. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Untrusted Search Path
mappings.mappingRationale: Trust in external search paths (DLL hijacking) typically abuses the loading mechanism for third-party components (#10) or is #1->#7.

mappings.cweName: Uncontrolled Search Path Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Uncontrolled search path element — attacker plants a malicious DLL/shared-library on a writable path, the OS loader loads it via search-order resolution. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (loader function abused); per R-EXEC the loaded code executes -> append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Unquoted Search Path or Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Unquoted Windows search path — spaces in the path cause Windows to try multiple binary candidates in sequence; attacker plants an executable matching one of the earlier candidates. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (loader function abused); per R-EXEC the loaded executable runs -> append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Deployment of Wrong Handler
mappings.mappingRationale: The wrong handler/MIME type processes the request, exposing source code or invoking an unintended function. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Missing Handler
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing handler is a robustness/code-quality defect; the resulting unhandled state's threat (if any) classifies under the specific failure mode.

mappings.cweName: Dangerous Signal Handler not Disabled During Sensitive Operations
mappings.mappingRationale: Dangerous signal handler not disabled during sensitive ops — handler races into the critical section. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unparsed Raw Web Content Delivery
mappings.mappingRationale: Source files are served raw instead of executed, exposing logic and embedded secrets. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of the upload function (#1) to introduce foreign code/malware (#7).

mappings.cweName: Improper Interaction Between Multiple Correctly-Behaving Entities
mappings.mappingRationale: Abstract category — improper interactions between multiple correctly-behaving entities (request-smuggling-class, parser-discrepancy-class). Specific cases classify at concrete child CWEs (CWE-436 Interpretation Conflict, CWE-444 HTTP Request Smuggling).

mappings.cweName: Interpretation Conflict
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw in parsing logic leading to bypass (e.g., HTTP smuggling).

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Model of Endpoint Features
mappings.mappingRationale: Abstract design defect (incomplete endpoint model). Specific consequences classify at the child level.

mappings.cweName: Behavioral Change in New Version or Environment
mappings.mappingRationale: Operational/behavioral change between versions — not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Expected Behavior Violation
mappings.mappingRationale: Abstract category for behavior-violation flaws. Classify at the specific deviation child CWE.

mappings.cweName: Unintended Proxy or Intermediary ('Confused Deputy')
mappings.mappingRationale: Abusing the deputy's legitimate functionality (#1) to perform unauthorized actions.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: HTTP response splitting
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated (rolled into CWE-113 'Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers'). Per Prohibited-verdict policy, deprecated entries map to N/A.

mappings.cweName: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')
mappings.mappingRationale: HTTP request smuggling — front-end (CDN, load balancer) and back-end (origin server) interpret request boundaries differently (CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE), letting an attacker hide a smuggled request inside a legitimate one. Server-role parsing flaw -> #2.

mappings.cweName: UI Discrepancy for Security Feature
mappings.mappingRationale: UI presents inconsistent state for a security feature (icon shows secure when it isn't, or vice versa) — enables user deception. Per ruling-2 -> #9.

mappings.cweName: Unimplemented or Unsupported Feature in UI
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (UI feature stub) — non-threat unless the unimplemented feature was a security control, in which case classify the missing control.

mappings.cweName: Obsolete Feature in UI
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (obsolete UI feature) — non-threat code-quality.

mappings.cweName: The UI Performs the Wrong Action
mappings.mappingRationale: UI control performs an action the user did not intend (mislabeled button, wrong default). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (the UI function executes the wrong logic relative to user intent).

mappings.cweName: Multiple Interpretations of UI Input
mappings.mappingRationale: UI input is interpreted differently in different contexts (Unicode normalization, locale), creating a security-relevant ambiguity. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: User Interface (UI) Misrepresentation of Critical Information
mappings.mappingRationale: UI misrepresents critical security information (URL spoofing in address bar, certificate UI manipulation) — primary phishing/deception vector. Per ruling-2 -> #9.

mappings.cweName: Insecure Default Variable Initialization
mappings.mappingRationale: Insecure default initialization of variables in server frameworks (default 'true', open mode). Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: External Initialization of Trusted Variables or Data Stores
mappings.mappingRationale: External initialization of trusted variables (CGI environment, shared memory) — attacker controls 'trusted' state. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Non-exit on Failed Initialization
mappings.mappingRationale: Initialization failure does not abort — server proceeds with partially-initialized state. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Missing Initialization of a Variable
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side variable not initialized — undefined values flow into security-relevant decisions. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Uninitialized Variable
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of uninitialized variable — undefined value flows into security-relevant logic. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Incorrect Initialization
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-665 (Improper Initialization).

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Cleanup
mappings.mappingRationale: Incomplete cleanup leaves sensitive data in resources (caches, buffers) for later attackers. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Cleanup on Thrown Exception
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper cleanup on thrown exception leaves resources in inconsistent state. Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Duplicate Key in Associative List (Alist)
mappings.mappingRationale: Duplicate key in associative list — lookup returns one of two values nondeterministically, sometimes exploitable. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Deletion of Data Structure Sentinel
mappings.mappingRationale: Sentinel deleted from data structure — iteration walks past expected boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Addition of Data Structure Sentinel
mappings.mappingRationale: Sentinel value spuriously added — iteration terminates early, skipping valid entries. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Return of Pointer Value Outside of Expected Range
mappings.mappingRationale: Pointer returned from a function points outside the expected range, propagating into UAF/OOB defects. Pointer-manipulation code implementation flaw (memory-safety adjacent). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of sizeof() on a Pointer Type
mappings.mappingRationale: sizeof() applied to a pointer (returns pointer size) where buffer size was intended — under-allocation. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Pointer Scaling
mappings.mappingRationale: Pointer scaling (pointer arithmetic) computed with wrong type granularity, producing OOB access. Pointer-manipulation code implementation flaw (memory-safety adjacent). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Pointer Subtraction to Determine Size
mappings.mappingRationale: Pointer-subtraction-as-size assumes contiguity; if pointers are from different allocations the result is undefined. Pointer-manipulation code implementation flaw (memory-safety adjacent). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection')
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client -> Malware
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw allowing attacker-chosen class/method instantiation via reflection. Common in Java servers (#2) and Android clients (#3). Per R-EXEC, reflective instantiation of attacker-selected code executes foreign code — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Modification of Assumed-Immutable Data (MAID)
mappings.mappingRationale: Data the application assumes is immutable can be modified by the attacker (cookies, hidden fields, client-side state), invalidating later trust decisions. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: External Control of Assumed-Immutable Web Parameter
mappings.mappingRationale: Web parameters the application assumes immutable (e.g., signed token used as a backup) can be tampered with by the attacker. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: PHP External Variable Modification
mappings.mappingRationale: PHP register_globals-style external variable modification — attacker query string parameters silently set internal variables. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Function with Inconsistent Implementations
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of a function with multiple inconsistent implementations across platforms/versions. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Undefined Behavior for Input to API
mappings.mappingRationale: Undefined behavior for input to API — caller passes values the API did not specify, producing implementation-defined results. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: NULL Pointer Dereference
mappings.mappingRationale: Null-pointer dereference — uncaught null check causes crash (DoS). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Obsolete Function
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (use of obsolete function). Threat (if any) is the specific weakness in the obsolete function.

mappings.cweName: Missing Default Case in Multiple Condition Expression
mappings.mappingRationale: Switch/case missing default case lets unexpected input fall through, leaving the function in an undefined state. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (logic gap in the function's control flow).

mappings.cweName: Signal Handler Use of a Non-reentrant Function
mappings.mappingRationale: Signal handler invokes a non-reentrant function (e.g., printf, malloc) — racing with main flow corrupts state. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role concurrency flaw).

mappings.cweName: Use of Incorrect Operator
mappings.mappingRationale: Wrong operator used in expression (& vs &&, | vs ||) — silent semantic change. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Assigning instead of Comparing
mappings.mappingRationale: Coding-level typo (= used where == intended) creates an unintended assignment in a conditional, often collapsing security checks. Decision tree Q2 (code implementation flaw) -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Comparing instead of Assigning
mappings.mappingRationale: Coding-level typo (== used where = intended) leaves intended assignment unperformed. Decision tree Q2 (code implementation flaw) -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Block Delimitation
mappings.mappingRationale: Block-delimitation mistake causing statements to fall outside their intended scope (e.g., Apple's goto-fail TLS bug skipping certificate validation). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Omitted Break Statement in Switch
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing break in a switch causes unintended fall-through into adjacent cases. Decision tree Q2 (code implementation flaw) -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Comparison of Classes by Name
mappings.mappingRationale: Comparing classes by string name allows attacker-controlled namespaces/class-loaders to spoof the expected class identity. Code implementation flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Package-level Scope
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/design issue (relying on package-level scope). No direct threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Data Element to Wrong Session
mappings.mappingRationale: Data is stored in a session/scope visible to the wrong user (e.g., cached in a shared session). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Active Debug Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Active debug code in production exposes internal functions and data. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (the debug function is reachable when it should not be).

mappings.cweName: Public cloneable() Method Without Final ('Object Hijack')
mappings.mappingRationale: Public cloneable() method without final lets an attacker subclass and override clone() to bypass invariants ('object hijacking'). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Use of Inner Class Containing Sensitive Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/design defect (inner class with sensitive data). Specific exposures classify at the child level.

mappings.cweName: Critical Public Variable Without Final Modifier
mappings.mappingRationale: Critical public variable without final modifier can be reassigned by other code, including subclasses, breaking invariants. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
mappings.mappingRationale: Trust acceptance event (#10): downloaded code is treated as authoritative without integrity verification, enabling tampered binaries/updates. Per R-EXEC, the downloaded code subsequently executes — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Private Data Structure Returned From A Public Method
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (returning private mutable data structure) — encapsulation defect, not a direct threat.

mappings.cweName: Public Data Assigned to Private Array-Typed Field
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (public assignment to private array field) — encapsulation defect.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
mappings.mappingRationale: Server discloses sensitive system information (paths, version, internal state) to unauthorized callers. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role implementation flaw in the disclosing function).

mappings.cweName: Cloneable Class Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (cloneable class with sensitive data) — defensive-programming concern.

mappings.cweName: Serializable Class Containing Sensitive Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (serializable class with sensitive data) — defensive-programming concern.

mappings.cweName: Public Static Final Field References Mutable Object
mappings.mappingRationale: Public static final field references a mutable object; the field reference is final but the underlying state can still be modified. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Trust Boundary Violation
mappings.mappingRationale: Abstract design concept (trust-boundary violation). Specific instances map to concrete CWEs (e.g., #1 missing-authz, #5 missing-encryption-on-cross-boundary).

mappings.cweName: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client -> Malware
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw deserializing attacker-controlled bytes into language objects, triggering gadget-chain code execution (e.g., Java/Python pickle). Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE. Per R-EXEC, append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Embedded Malicious Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Presence of malicious code implies a supply chain or insider threat (#10).

mappings.cweName: Trojan Horse
mappings.mappingRationale: Malicious code present in the product — trojan horse — code that masquerades as legitimate functionality. Decision tree Q6 -> #7. (Per Axiom III, presence of malware is itself the threat action; the supply-chain-insertion event is captured by #10 in the chain.)

mappings.cweName: Non-Replicating Malicious Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Malicious code present in the product — non-replicating malicious code. Decision tree Q6 -> #7. (Per Axiom III, presence of malware is itself the threat action; the supply-chain-insertion event is captured by #10 in the chain.)

mappings.cweName: Replicating Malicious Code (Virus or Worm)
mappings.mappingRationale: Malicious code present in the product — replicating malicious code (virus or worm) — adds R-EXEC propagation step but the cluster classification is the malware presence itself. Decision tree Q6 -> #7. (Per Axiom III, presence of malware is itself the threat action; the supply-chain-insertion event is captured by #10 in the chain.)

mappings.cweName: Trapdoor
mappings.mappingRationale: Trapdoor/backdoor inserted into the product before delivery — supply-chain insertion at the trust-acceptance event. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: Logic/Time Bomb
mappings.mappingRationale: Logic/time bomb inserted into code awaiting a trigger condition — supply-chain or insider insertion. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: Spyware
mappings.mappingRationale: Malicious code present in the product — spyware — covert observation/exfiltration code. Decision tree Q6 -> #7. (Per Axiom III, presence of malware is itself the threat action; the supply-chain-insertion event is captured by #10 in the chain.)

mappings.cweName: Covert Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Covert channel — communication path used outside its intended purpose to leak data. Often physical / side-channel in nature, though pure-software covert channels exist (these stay in #2|#3 at instance level). Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Covert Storage Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Covert storage channel — data leaked via shared storage that the attacker can observe (cache, registers, side memory). Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Covert Timing Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-385 (Covert Timing Channel).

mappings.cweName: .NET Misconfiguration: Use of Impersonation
mappings.mappingRationale: ASP.NET impersonation misconfiguration runs code under a different identity than intended. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Weak Password Requirements
mappings.mappingRationale: Weak password requirements (low minimum length, no complexity) yield credentials trivially brute-forceable offline. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
mappings.mappingRationale: Credentials stored or transmitted without sufficient protection are recoverable for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Unprotected Transport of Credentials
mappings.mappingRationale: Credentials transmitted over an unprotected channel — interceptor recovers them and subsequently applies them per R-CRED. Decision tree Q4 -> #5 (acquisition step); subsequent credential application is #4.

mappings.cweName: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Cache containing sensitive information accessible to other principals (proxy cache, browser cache, shared memory). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Web Browser Cache Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Browser cache contains sensitive information that other clients can retrieve (e.g., shared kiosk, malware reading cache files). Client-role implementation flaw -> #3.

mappings.cweName: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information in an Environment Variable
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via environment variables exposed in process listings or core dumps. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Version-Control Repository to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
mappings.mappingRationale: Version-control directories (.git, .svn) under the web root expose source code and history. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the file-serving function).

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Core Dump File to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via core dump file accessible to unauthorized parties. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Access Control List Files to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
mappings.mappingRationale: Access-control list files (.htaccess, web.config) are themselves fetchable, revealing the access policy. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Backup File to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
mappings.mappingRationale: Backup files (config.bak, .swp) under the web root are fetchable, exposing the backed-up content. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Test Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via test code shipped in production with hardcoded values, debug endpoints, or sensitive sample data. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via application log files containing credentials, tokens, PII, or query parameters. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Information Exposure Through Server Log Files
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File).

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Information Exposure Through Debug Log Files
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-532.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Information Through Shell Error Message
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via shell error messages bubbled up to the user. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Servlet Runtime Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via servlet runtime error messages containing internal context. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Java Runtime Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Java runtime error message contains sensitive information (stack traces, class names, paths). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive information stored in externally-accessible location (world-readable file, public S3 bucket, Android external storage). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Persistent Cookies Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Persistent cookies hold sensitive information that survives session end and is exposed to local malware or shared-machine attackers. Client-role implementation flaw -> #3.

mappings.cweName: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via source code shipped in deployment artifacts. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in an Include File
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via include files (e.g., config.inc.php) accessible via the web server. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Information Exposure Through Cleanup Log Files
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-532.

mappings.cweName: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
mappings.mappingRationale: Singleton pattern without synchronization in multi-threaded context. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Missing Standardized Error Handling Mechanism
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (inconsistent error-handling). Specific exploitable consequences classify at the child level.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Use of Dynamic Class Loading
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into broader dynamic-class-loading CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Suspicious Comment
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via suspicious comments in shipped source code (TODO, password, API key). Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Hard-coded, Security-relevant Constants
mappings.mappingRationale: Too generic — the constant could be a credential (#4), a crypto key (#4/#5), an authorization flag (#1), or a logic value with no direct cluster. Classify at the more specific child CWE (e.g., CWE-798 hard-coded credentials).

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing
mappings.mappingRationale: Web server directory listing is enabled, revealing files and structure. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the listing feature).

mappings.cweName: Missing Password Field Masking
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing password-field masking — password visible on screen enables shoulder surfing, screen-recording malware, and remote-desktop snooping. Physical/local observation -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Server-generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side information-leak variant — sensitive data exposed via server-generated error pages with stack traces or configuration. Per Axiom III the leak is the consequence; the cause is the implementation flaw in the emitting function. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Behavior Order: Authorization Before Parsing and Canonicalization
mappings.mappingRationale: Authorization runs before parsing/canonicalization, letting an attacker craft input that authorizes pre-canonicalization but executes a different operation post-canonicalization. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties
mappings.mappingRationale: Files or directories accessible to external parties (network share, world-readable mount, public S3 bucket). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the storage function's access policy).

mappings.cweName: Command Shell in Externally Accessible Directory
mappings.mappingRationale: Command shell present in an externally accessible directory — typically a backdoor artifact (deployed as #10) or a leftover dev tool. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Not Using Input Validation Framework
mappings.mappingRationale: Skipping the validation framework leaves request inputs unfiltered, enabling server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) injection/exploit per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Misconfiguration: Plaintext Password in Configuration File
mappings.mappingRationale: Plaintext password in J2EE configuration is recoverable for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 → #4.

mappings.cweName: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Use of Identity Impersonation
mappings.mappingRationale: ASP.NET Identity Impersonation misconfiguration runs the request under an unintended identity. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Use of getlogin() in Multithreaded Application
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of getlogin() in a multi-threaded application — getlogin returns the login of the controlling terminal, which is shared and racy. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of umask() with chmod-style Argument
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of umask() with chmod-style argument — developer passes 0644 thinking it sets that mode, but umask interprets it as the mask, producing 0133 (the inverse). Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Dead Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Dead code — code-quality issue. Not a threat unless the dead code becomes reachable, in which case classify by the specific weakness then.

mappings.cweName: Return of Stack Variable Address
mappings.mappingRationale: Returning the address of a stack variable — caller dereferences a stale stack frame. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Assignment to Variable without Use
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (assignment without use). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: SQL Injection: Hibernate
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side SQL injection in Hibernate/HQL — attacker payload alters the HQL query semantics. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking
mappings.mappingRationale: Cookies are trusted as integrity-protected when they are not (no signature/HMAC). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (parameter tampering via the cookie).

mappings.cweName: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled SQL Primary Key
mappings.mappingRationale: User-controlled parameter (often a primary-key ID) is used directly in an SQL WHERE clause for authorization, letting an attacker reach other users' rows. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (IDOR via the query function).

mappings.cweName: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
mappings.mappingRationale: Unsynchronized access to shared data in multi-threaded context. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: finalize() Method Without super.finalize()
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (finalize() missing super.finalize()). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Expression is Always False
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (always-false expression — dead branch). Not a threat in itself.

mappings.cweName: Expression is Always True
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (always-true expression — vacuous check). The associated security check being vacuous is a separate cause; classify there.

mappings.cweName: Call to Thread run() instead of start()
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/logic bug (Thread.run vs. Thread.start). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Improper Following of Specification by Caller
mappings.mappingRationale: Generic code-quality concept covering many possible downstream weaknesses; no single cluster fits. Classify at the specific spec-deviation child CWE.

mappings.cweName: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Synchronization Primitives
mappings.mappingRationale: EJB best-practice violation (synchronization primitives in EJB). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: EJB Bad Practices: Use of AWT Swing
mappings.mappingRationale: EJB best-practice violation (AWT/Swing primitives in EJB context). Non-threat code-quality issue with no defensible threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Java I/O
mappings.mappingRationale: EJB best-practice violation (direct java.io in EJB). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Sockets
mappings.mappingRationale: EJB best-practice violation (direct sockets in EJB). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: EJB Bad Practices: Use of Class Loader
mappings.mappingRationale: EJB best-practice violation (custom class loader in EJB). Non-threat code-quality issue.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Bad Practices: Non-serializable Object Stored in Session
mappings.mappingRationale: J2EE best-practice violation (non-serializable in session). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: clone() Method Without super.clone()
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (clone() missing super.clone()). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Object Model Violation: Just One of Equals and Hashcode Defined
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (only one of equals/hashCode overridden). Not a threat.

mappings.cweName: Array Declared Public, Final, and Static
mappings.mappingRationale: Public final static array — the reference is final but the array contents are mutable, so other code can rewrite the entries. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: finalize() Method Declared Public
mappings.mappingRationale: finalize() declared public lets external code call it directly, double-running cleanup or invoking it at unexpected times. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Return Inside Finally Block
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/logic bug (return inside finally). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Empty Synchronized Block
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (empty synchronized block). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Explicit Call to Finalize()
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (explicit finalize() call). Not a generic vulnerability.

mappings.cweName: Assignment of a Fixed Address to a Pointer
mappings.mappingRationale: Assigning a fixed (often null or magic) address to a pointer — dereference accesses a controlled location. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Attempt to Access Child of a Non-structure Pointer
mappings.mappingRationale: Access of a child member through a non-structure pointer (e.g., dereferencing a void* as a struct) — type-confusion-class memory error. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Call to Non-ubiquitous API
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/portability issue (call to non-ubiquitous API). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Free of Memory not on the Heap
mappings.mappingRationale: Free of memory not on the heap (stack address, static address, mid-allocation pointer) corrupts allocator state. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Sensitive Data Storage in Improperly Locked Memory
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw. Vital for Client apps (#3) to prevent sensitive data from swapping to disk.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Authentication Bypass Issues
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-287 (Improper Authentication) family.

mappings.cweName: Authentication Bypass: OpenSSL CTX Object Modified after SSL Objects are Created
mappings.mappingRationale: OpenSSL CTX object modified after SSL_set_fd / SSL_new — context changes silently ignored. Code implementation flaw in API usage. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: J2EE Framework: Saving Unserializable Objects to Disk
mappings.mappingRationale: J2EE framework saves unserializable objects to disk/session — runtime fails when restoring, causing DoS. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Comparison of Object References Instead of Object Contents
mappings.mappingRationale: Comparing object references instead of object content lets logically-equal-but-differently-allocated objects fail equality and bypass intended logic. Code implementation flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Incorrect Semantic Object Comparison
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-595 (Comparison of Object References Instead of Object Contents).

mappings.cweName: Use of Wrong Operator in String Comparison
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of == instead of .equals() in string comparison (Java) compares interned references, not content; auth tokens or secret values can compare unequal even when content matches expectations, or vice versa. Code implementation flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive data in URL query string sent via GET — query strings persist in browser history, server logs, referers, intermediaries. Server-role implementation flaw -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Missing Validation of OpenSSL Certificate
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing OpenSSL certificate validation — TLS connection accepts any certificate. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Uncaught Exception in Servlet
mappings.mappingRationale: Uncaught exception in servlet bubbles to the container, often producing a default error page that leaks stack traces. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
mappings.mappingRationale: Open-redirect: the redirect function accepts an untrusted destination, abusable for phishing chains and OAuth-token theft. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side security relies on client-side enforcement (JS validation, hidden flag) which the attacker bypasses by submitting directly. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Use of Client-Side Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication is performed only on the client (e.g., JS check) and not enforced server-side; trivially bypassable. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Multiple Binds to the Same Port
mappings.mappingRationale: Multiple binds to the same port — the second bind may take over message routing if the first crashes, enabling port hijacking. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
mappings.mappingRationale: Attacker-controlled input determines loop iteration count. This is parameter tampering that abuses the loop's functional logic (#1), not capacity exhaustion. The loop condition is functional logic being manipulated via unexpected input values, not a finite resource being overwhelmed by volume.

mappings.cweName: Public Static Final Field References Mutable Object
mappings.mappingRationale: Public static final field references a mutable object; the field is constant but its target's state can be mutated. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Struts: Non-private Field in ActionForm Class
mappings.mappingRationale: Struts ActionForm with non-private fields exposes business state to direct manipulation. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Double-Checked Locking
mappings.mappingRationale: Double-checked locking pattern is broken on memory models without proper barriers. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere
mappings.mappingRationale: Externally-controlled reference to a resource in another sphere (parent class for IDOR, SSRF, path traversal logic). Specific cases classify at child CWEs. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side XML External Entity (XXE) — parser resolves DOCTYPE-declared external entities, fetching attacker-controlled URLs (file://, http://). Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Authorization of Index Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Index of sensitive items (search index, cache) returns entries the user is not authorized to view. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Session Expiration
mappings.mappingRationale: Insufficient session expiration extends the window in which a stolen session token remains valid for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
mappings.mappingRationale: The Secure attribute is a legitimate configuration parameter that was incorrectly set. This is a configuration/functional scope issue (#1) where the cookie security setting is misconfigured, allowing the cookie to be sent over unencrypted connections. The attacker abuses the insecure configuration.

mappings.cweName: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code Comments
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive information in source code comments shipped to clients (HTML/JS comments) or visible after deployment. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Identification of Uploaded File Variables (PHP)
mappings.mappingRationale: Incomplete identification of uploaded file variables — server-side file-upload handler does not consistently identify which inputs are files vs. metadata, enabling variable injection. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Reachable Assertion
mappings.mappingRationale: Reachable assertion on attacker input — assert() triggers process termination, causing DoS. Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Exposed Unsafe ActiveX Method
mappings.mappingRationale: ActiveX control exposes an unsafe method that any web page can invoke once the control is instantiated. Client-role component vulnerability -> #3.

mappings.cweName: Dangling Database Cursor ('Cursor Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Dangling database cursor (cursor injection) — server reuses cursors across user contexts, letting one user observe another's data. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Unverified Password Change
mappings.mappingRationale: Password change endpoint does not verify the current user's identity (no current-password check, no reauth). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the password-change function).

mappings.cweName: Variable Extraction Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Variable extraction error — server-side use of extract()/import_request_variables() lets attacker query string set internal variables. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Function Hook Arguments
mappings.mappingRationale: Function-hook arguments not validated — hook callback receives attacker-controllable parameters that bypass higher-level checks. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Unsafe ActiveX Control Marked Safe For Scripting
mappings.mappingRationale: ActiveX control marked Safe-For-Scripting despite exposing dangerous functionality — any web page can drive the dangerous behavior. Client-role component vulnerability -> #3.

mappings.cweName: Executable Regular Expression Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Executable regex (e.g., /e modifier in PHP preg_replace) — the replacement is evaluated as code, enabling code injection. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-side); see CWE-94 / CWE-95 for the R-EXEC chain.

mappings.cweName: Permissive Regular Expression
mappings.mappingRationale: Regex used as a security validator is too permissive, accepting inputs that should have been rejected. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the validation function via inputs the regex permits).

mappings.cweName: Null Byte Interaction Error (Poison Null Byte)
mappings.mappingRationale: Null-byte interaction error (poison null byte) — language/API mismatch in null-terminator handling. Affects PHP/C boundaries (#2) and Java/JNI (#2 or #3). Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Dynamic Variable Evaluation
mappings.mappingRationale: Dynamic variable evaluation (PHP $$var, register_globals) — attacker query parameter sets a variable name the program then dereferences. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
mappings.mappingRationale: Function call with incorrectly specified arguments — wrong literal, wrong constant, wrong flag passed at the call site. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Not Failing Securely ('Failing Open')
mappings.mappingRationale: On error, security checks default to permitting the action instead of denying. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the default-permit branch of the security function).

mappings.cweName: Unnecessary Complexity in Protection Mechanism (Not Using 'Economy of Mechanism')
mappings.mappingRationale: Design principle violation, not a concrete weakness. Specific bugs introduced by the complexity classify at their respective child CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Not Using Complete Mediation
mappings.mappingRationale: Authorization checks are not applied at every access path (incomplete mediation), letting an attacker reach resources via unchecked paths. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
mappings.mappingRationale: Authorization decision uses a user-controlled key (record ID); the attacker substitutes another user's key (IDOR). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
mappings.mappingRationale: Abuse of the password-recovery function (weak verification, predictable reset token, security-question guessing) to reset another user's password. Decision tree Q9 → #1. Per Axiom III, account takeover is the consequence; the cause is the recovery-flow logic flaw.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Names for Files and Other Resources
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side filename / resource-name validation flaw — names with traversal sequences or special characters bypass the restriction. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: External Control of Critical State Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Critical state data (auth status, role, price) is stored in attacker-modifiable locations (cookies, hidden fields, query strings). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (parameter tampering).

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side XPath injection — attacker payload modifies the XPath query semantics, exfiltrating XML store contents. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side HTTP header injection — unsanitized newlines in response headers enable header smuggling and response splitting. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Overly Restrictive Account Lockout Mechanism
mappings.mappingRationale: Attacker abuses the legitimate account lockout function beyond its intended scope (#1) to deny access to legitimate users. The lockout mechanism works as designed; the attacker manipulates it for malicious purposes. This is functional scope abuse, not overwhelming finite capacity.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on File Name or Extension of Externally-Supplied File
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side file-upload check that trusts the externally-supplied filename or extension instead of inspecting content. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Non-Canonical URL Paths for Authorization Decisions
mappings.mappingRationale: Authorization decisions use the URL as-typed instead of canonicalized form, allowing bypass via path-equivalent variants (./, %2e%2e/, double slashes). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Use of Privileged APIs
mappings.mappingRationale: Privileged API used incorrectly (parameters not validated, called from the wrong context) lets an attacker invoke the privileged action. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Obfuscation or Encryption of Security-Relevant Inputs without Integrity Checking
mappings.mappingRationale: Security relies on obfuscation/encoding instead of cryptographic verification; the obfuscation is reversible by the attacker. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Trusting HTTP Permission Methods on the Server Side
mappings.mappingRationale: Server trusts HTTP method (GET vs. POST, PUT, DELETE) for security decisions even though the client controls the method. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of WSDL File Containing Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: WSDL file exposes sensitive endpoint/parameter information that aids reconnaissance and exploitation. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions ('XQuery Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side XQuery injection — attacker payload modifies XQuery semantics, exfiltrating XML store contents. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Isolation or Compartmentalization
mappings.mappingRationale: Components are not sufficiently isolated, letting compromise of one component reach functions in another. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on a Single Factor in a Security Decision
mappings.mappingRationale: Security decision depends on a single factor (single password, single token); compromise of that factor grants full access. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Psychological Acceptability
mappings.mappingRationale: Security mechanisms users find onerous get bypassed or worked around, increasing the surface for user-deception attacks. Per ruling-2 enabling-condition policy → #9.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Security Through Obscurity
mappings.mappingRationale: Design anti-principle, not a concrete weakness. The actual exploit cluster depends on what the obscured mechanism turns out to protect (a credential, a key, a function) — classify at that level.

mappings.cweName: Violation of Secure Design Principles
mappings.mappingRationale: Violation of secure-design principles (meta-weakness covering Saltzer-Schroeder principles like least-privilege, complete-mediation). Specific exploitable consequences classify at concrete child CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Improper Synchronization
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for synchronization flaws (race conditions, lock errors). Specific cases at child CWEs. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role default).

mappings.cweName: Use of a Non-reentrant Function in a Concurrent Context
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of a non-reentrant function in a concurrent context (e.g., gmtime() in multi-threaded code). Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for resource-lifetime flaws. Specific cases at child CWEs (CWE-401, 415, 416, 825). Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role default).

mappings.cweName: Improper Initialization
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for initialization flaws. Specific cases at child CWEs. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role default).

mappings.cweName: Operation on Resource in Wrong Phase of Lifetime
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for resource-lifetime-phase flaws. Specific cases at child CWEs. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role default).

mappings.cweName: Improper Locking
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing/incorrect locking around shared state allows concurrent corruption (race-window exploitation). Server-role concurrency flaw -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for resource-exposure flaws (resource visible to wrong sphere). Specific cases classify at child CWEs (CWE-200, 219, 552). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres
mappings.mappingRationale: A resource intended for one sphere is incorrectly transferred into another, exposing functions to callers that should not reach them. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Always-Incorrect Control Flow Implementation
mappings.mappingRationale: Control-flow logic that always takes a wrong branch (e.g., security check unreachable). Server-role implementation flaw -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Lack of Administrator Control over Security
mappings.mappingRationale: Manageability defect — admin cannot configure security to fit the deployment. Does not itself constitute a threat action against any single cluster.

mappings.cweName: Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release
mappings.mappingRationale: Use-after-free / use-after-release of a freed object. Memory-safety code flaw - server-role (#2, e.g., HTTP daemon) or client-role (#3, e.g., browser engine) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: External Influence of Sphere Definition
mappings.mappingRationale: Attacker-influenced sphere definition lets the attacker reposition trust boundaries to invoke functions across them. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Uncontrolled Recursion
mappings.mappingRationale: Uncontrolled recursion — input drives recursion depth, causing stack exhaustion. Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Multiple Operations on Resource in Single-Operation Context
mappings.mappingRationale: Multiple operations performed where the API contract assumes one (double free, double init), corrupting state. Server-role implementation flaw -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of potentially-dangerous functions (strcpy, gets, atoi without overflow check). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Integer Overflow to Buffer Overflow
mappings.mappingRationale: Arithmetic implementation flaw. A primary vector for Client-side exploitation (#3) (e.g., media parsing).

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
mappings.mappingRationale: Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Calculation
mappings.mappingRationale: Arithmetic implementation flaw. Calculation errors affect logic and safety in both Server (#2) and Client (#3) applications.

mappings.cweName: Function Call With Incorrect Order of Arguments
mappings.mappingRationale: Function call with arguments in wrong order — silent semantic change. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Provision of Specified Functionality
mappings.mappingRationale: Generic code-correctness defect. The exploitable cluster depends on what specified functionality is incorrect. Classify at the more specific child CWE.

mappings.cweName: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
mappings.mappingRationale: Function call with incorrect number of arguments. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Function Call With Incorrect Argument Type
mappings.mappingRationale: Function call with incorrect argument type — coerced/lossy conversion at the call site. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Function Call With Incorrectly Specified Argument Value
mappings.mappingRationale: Function call with incorrectly specified argument value (literal vs. variable, wrong constant). Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Function Call With Incorrect Variable or Reference as Argument
mappings.mappingRationale: Function call with incorrect variable or reference (wrong argument bound to the parameter slot). Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Permission Race Condition During Resource Copy
mappings.mappingRationale: Race between a permission check and a resource copy — privileged operation completes against the post-race state. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw. Null pointer dereferences cause crashes (DoS) in Client applications (#3) as well as Servers.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Control Flow Management
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for control-flow management flaws. Specific cases at child CWEs. Decision tree Q2 -> #2 (server-role default).

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Denylist to Cross-Site Scripting
mappings.mappingRationale: XSS-specific incomplete denylist — denylist of dangerous patterns is incomplete, letting variant payloads through. Sibling of CWE-184 but XSS-scoped. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Protection Mechanism Failure
mappings.mappingRationale: Abstract category — protection mechanism failure umbrella. Specific failures classify at concrete child CWEs (CWE-862 missing-authz, CWE-307 brute-force, CWE-311 missing-encryption, etc.).

mappings.cweName: Use of Multiple Resources with Duplicate Identifier
mappings.mappingRationale: Multiple resources share the same identifier, letting an attacker substitute one for another in operations that resolve the identifier. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Use of Low-Level Functionality
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of low-level functionality (raw memory ops, direct hardware access) where higher-level abstractions would be safer. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Behavior Order
mappings.mappingRationale: Behavior order mistakes (e.g., authorization-after-parsing, log-after-action). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (the function executes in the wrong sequence relative to its security checks).

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Comparison
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for incorrect-comparison flaws (timing-attack, type-confusion comparison, partial match). Specific cases classify at child CWEs. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Execution After Redirect (EAR)
mappings.mappingRationale: Code continues executing after issuing a redirect that should have terminated the request, letting subsequent statements run with the unredirected state. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Software Development
mappings.mappingRationale: Organizational view (CWE-699 Software Development view), not a concrete weakness. Per R-Q0, view nodes are Prohibited.

mappings.cweName: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw. Poor error handling leads to insecure states in any software context (#2 or #3).

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
mappings.mappingRationale: Incorrect type conversion / type confusion — wrong type interpretation propagates to memory access or logic. Common in JIT engines and dynamic languages. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Control Flow Scoping
mappings.mappingRationale: Control-flow scoping mistakes (missing/extra return, fall-through) skip security checks. Server-role implementation flaw -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference
mappings.mappingRationale: A name/reference resolves to an unintended target (path resolution, namespace collision). Server-role implementation flaw -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for improper-neutralization (injection) flaws. Specific cases at child CWEs (CWE-77 command, CWE-78 OS command, CWE-79 XSS, CWE-89 SQL, CWE-94 code, CWE-95 eval). Decision tree Q2 with R-EXEC where execution is enabled.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Ownership Assignment
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource is created with the wrong owner, exposing it to unintended principals. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper adherence to coding standards — generic code-quality umbrella with no specific threat cluster. Specific exploitable defects classify at child CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Critical resource (file, directory, IPC object) created with permissions allowing unintended principals — abuse of the resource's access function. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Compiler optimization removes/modifies security-relevant code (sibling of CWE-1037 — explicit memset of sensitive buffer optimized away because the buffer is dead). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
mappings.mappingRationale: Dangerous methods/functions are exposed without sufficient access control (debug API, admin RPC, unprotected JNI). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper check for unusual/exceptional conditions — fail-open code path. Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw. Failing to handle exceptions correctly affects Client (#3) stability/security.

mappings.cweName: Missing Custom Error Page
mappings.mappingRationale: Default error pages reveal stack traces and configuration. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the default error-handler function in a context where it should not surface internals).

mappings.cweName: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation ('Algorithm Downgrade')
mappings.mappingRationale: Algorithm-downgrade attack: attacker manipulates protocol negotiation to force selection of a weaker cipher/hash, then exploits the weakened channel. Per ruling-2 (enabling-condition policy) and Q4 (communication-path weakness) -> #5.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
mappings.mappingRationale: Reliance on undefined / unspecified / implementation-defined behavior — security-relevant decisions depend on non-deterministic outcomes. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt
mappings.mappingRationale: Unsalted password hashes are recoverable via precomputed (rainbow) tables, exposing credentials for impersonation. Per ruling-2 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt
mappings.mappingRationale: Predictable salts collapse password-hash protection back to rainbow-table-tractable, exposing credentials for impersonation. Per ruling-2 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Free of Pointer not at Start of Buffer
mappings.mappingRationale: Free of pointer not at start of buffer corrupts allocator metadata. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Mismatched Memory Management Routines
mappings.mappingRationale: Mismatched memory-management routines (free() on new[]'d memory, malloc + delete) corrupts allocator state. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference
mappings.mappingRationale: Release of invalid pointer or reference (already-freed, mid-allocation, stack address). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Multiple locks of a critical resource (e.g., mutex acquired twice) — leads to deadlock and DoS. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Multiple Unlocks of a Critical Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Multiple unlocks of a critical resource — undefined-behavior in pthreads, deadlock or corruption in others. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Critical Data Element Declared Public
mappings.mappingRationale: Critical data element (config, secret, security flag) declared public, mutable by any caller. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Access to Critical Private Variable via Public Method
mappings.mappingRationale: Critical private variable accessible via a public method (getter/setter), bypassing intended encapsulation. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Short Circuit Evaluation
mappings.mappingRationale: Incorrect short-circuit evaluation (e.g., && precedence vs. function call ordering) yields unintended logic. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Uncontrolled File Descriptor Consumption
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated (rolled into CWE-770 'Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling'). Per Prohibited-verdict policy, deprecated entries map to N/A.

mappings.cweName: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — allocation of resources without limit/throttle — attacker drives unbounded resource creation. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Missing Reference to Active Allocated Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — missing reference to active allocated resource — orphaned resource cannot be released. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — missing release of resource after effective lifetime — resource leak accumulates over time. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Missing Reference to Active File Descriptor or Handle
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — missing reference to active file descriptor / handle — handles leak. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Allocation of File Descriptors or Handles Without Limits or Throttling
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — allocation of file descriptors / handles without limit. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — missing release of file descriptor / handle after effective lifetime. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — recursive entity references in DTD (Billion Laughs / XML bomb) explode parser memory. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Regular Expression without Anchors
mappings.mappingRationale: Regex without ^/$ anchors matches the pattern as a substring instead of the full input, letting attacker payloads slip past validation. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Logging
mappings.mappingRationale: Insufficient logging is a detection/forensics gap (per Axiom III, an absence of observability), not a threat action.

mappings.cweName: Logging of Excessive Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — logging of excessive data fills disk / log-aggregation pipeline. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP
mappings.mappingRationale: Textbook RSA without OAEP padding is vulnerable to chosen-ciphertext / Bleichenbacher-style attacks, recovering plaintext for an interceptor. Per ruling-2 → #5.

mappings.cweName: Improper Address Validation in IOCTL with METHOD_NEITHER I/O Control Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Kernel/driver IOCTL with METHOD_NEITHER fails to validate user-supplied addresses, enabling kernel memory access. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Exposed IOCTL with Insufficient Access Control
mappings.mappingRationale: IOCTL exposed without sufficient access control lets unprivileged callers invoke driver/kernel functionality. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Operator Precedence Logic Error
mappings.mappingRationale: Operator-precedence error — expression evaluates differently than the developer intended, often inverting a security check. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking in a Security Decision
mappings.mappingRationale: Cookies trusted as integrity-protected without validation/HMAC, abusable via parameter tampering. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Use of Path Manipulation Function without Maximum-sized Buffer
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of path-manipulation functions without maximum-sized destination buffer leads to overflow when source path is longer than expected. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Access of Memory Location Before Start of Buffer
mappings.mappingRationale: Memory access before the start of the buffer — pointer arithmetic produces an address below the allocation. Memory-safety code flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Out-of-bounds Write
mappings.mappingRationale: Out-of-bounds write — write past allocation boundary corrupts adjacent state; primary exploitation vector for browser/PDF/media-parser RCEs. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Access of Memory Location After End of Buffer
mappings.mappingRationale: Memory access after the end of the buffer — pointer arithmetic produces an address past the allocation. Memory-safety code flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — memory allocation with attacker-supplied excessive size value. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Improper Filtering of Special Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization/filtering bypass — code implementation flaw where the filter fails to neutralize attacker inputs. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Filtering of Special Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization/filtering bypass — code implementation flaw where the filter fails to neutralize attacker inputs. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Filtering of One or More Instances of Special Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization/filtering bypass — code implementation flaw where the filter fails to neutralize attacker inputs. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Only Filtering One Instance of a Special Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization/filtering bypass — code implementation flaw where the filter fails to neutralize attacker inputs. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Filtering of Multiple Instances of Special Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization/filtering bypass — code implementation flaw where the filter fails to neutralize attacker inputs. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Only Filtering Special Elements at a Specified Location
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization/filtering bypass — code implementation flaw where the filter fails to neutralize attacker inputs. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Only Filtering Special Elements Relative to a Marker
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization/filtering bypass — code implementation flaw where the filter fails to neutralize attacker inputs. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Only Filtering Special Elements at an Absolute Position
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization filter only checks an absolute position (e.g., 'no quote at index 0') instead of all positions — payloads at other positions slip through. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
mappings.mappingRationale: Hard-coded credentials baked into the product (passwords, API keys, cryptographic keys) — once extracted from binaries/firmware, every deployment becomes impersonable. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Improper Control of Interaction Frequency
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing rate-limiting / lockout permits unbounded interaction. Authentication endpoints → #4 (credential brute force / impersonation); resource endpoints → #6 (flooding / DoS). Per ruling-2 enabling-condition policy.

mappings.cweName: Guessable CAPTCHA
mappings.mappingRationale: CAPTCHA's challenge space is small or solvable by automation, letting attackers bypass the human-verification function. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value
mappings.mappingRationale: Buffer access uses wrong length (e.g., source size for destination access). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Buffer Access Using Size of Source Buffer
