mappings.mappingRationale: Buffer accessed using size of source buffer rather than destination capacity. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
mappings.mappingRationale: Security decisions depend on attacker-influenceable inputs (HTTP headers, cookies, client-asserted attributes). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Missing Synchronization
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing synchronization on shared data. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Synchronization
mappings.mappingRationale: Incorrect synchronization (wrong lock, wrong scope) leaves shared state mutable. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Untrusted Pointer Dereference
mappings.mappingRationale: Untrusted-pointer dereference — pointer value comes from external input. Pointer-manipulation code implementation flaw (memory-safety adjacent). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Out-of-range Pointer Offset
mappings.mappingRationale: Out-of-range pointer offset — pointer arithmetic produces address outside the original allocation. Pointer-manipulation code implementation flaw (memory-safety adjacent). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Access of Uninitialized Pointer
mappings.mappingRationale: Access of uninitialized pointer — wild dereference. Pointer-manipulation code implementation flaw (memory-safety adjacent). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Expired Pointer Dereference
mappings.mappingRationale: Expired (already-freed) pointer dereferenced — UAF variant. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Premature Release of Resource During Expected Lifetime
mappings.mappingRationale: Premature release of a resource that other code still references — UAF / dangling-handle precursor. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side improper control of XML DTD — DOCTYPE declarations are processed without restriction, enabling XXE-style attacks. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Signal Handler with Functionality that is not Asynchronous-Safe
mappings.mappingRationale: Signal handler invokes async-signal-unsafe functions, causing reentrance into non-reentrant code. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
mappings.mappingRationale: Trust acceptance event (#10): the product loads functionality (library, script, plugin) from outside its intended security domain. Per R-EXEC, included functionality runs in the host's execution context — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
mappings.mappingRationale: Trust acceptance event (#10): the page imports executable functionality (script, widget) from an untrusted external sphere. Per R-EXEC, the included script runs in the page context — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Signal Handler Function Associated with Multiple Signals
mappings.mappingRationale: One signal-handler function registered for multiple signals leaves it unable to disambiguate context. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unlock of a Resource that is not Locked
mappings.mappingRationale: Unlock of a resource that was not locked — undefined behavior in pthreads, exception in many lock APIs. Code implementation flaw — server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Deadlock
mappings.mappingRationale: Deadlock — threads wait on each other indefinitely. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Iteration
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class for excessive-iteration / infinite-loop flaws. Specific cases at child CWEs (CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion, CWE-835 infinite loop). Resource exhaustion / denial of service — unbounded iteration. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
mappings.mappingRationale: Loop with unreachable exit condition — infinite loop on attacker input causes DoS. Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Password Hash Instead of Password for Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication accepts the password hash directly (pass-the-hash) rather than requiring a plaintext password to verify against the hash. Per ruling-1, this is auth-LOGIC abuse (the auth function accepts the wrong credential form) -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action
mappings.mappingRationale: An action that should be performed at most once (file upload, transaction, vote) can be replayed because the function does not enforce uniqueness. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Inappropriate Encoding for Output Context
mappings.mappingRationale: Output emitted with encoding inappropriate for its context (HTML-encoded value placed in JS context, URL-encoded value placed in attribute) — the wrong encoding does not neutralize the right special characters. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Numeric Range Comparison Without Minimum Check
mappings.mappingRationale: Numeric-range comparison without minimum check accepts negative values where a positive bound was expected. Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow
mappings.mappingRationale: Business workflow steps (e.g., order -> pay -> ship) can be invoked out of sequence because the function does not enforce the workflow state machine. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Placement of User into Incorrect Group
mappings.mappingRationale: Group/role assignment places user in the wrong group, granting unintended access. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
mappings.mappingRationale: Type confusion — accessing a resource as the wrong type. Canonical example: V8/SpiderMonkey JIT type-confusion RCEs (#3); also occurs in server-side parsers (#2). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Missing Authorization
mappings.mappingRationale: A function performs a sensitive action without checking authorization at all. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Authorization
mappings.mappingRationale: An authorization check exists but evaluates incorrectly (wrong role compared, wrong resource referenced). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Use of Uninitialized Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of uninitialized resource — undefined values propagate into security-relevant decisions. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Missing Initialization of Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing initialization of a resource — operations on the resource encounter undefined state. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Expired File Descriptor
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of expired (closed/freed) file descriptor — recycled FD points to a different resource. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Update of Reference Count
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper reference-count update produces premature free or unbounded leak — UAF or memory exhaustion. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Hidden Functionality
mappings.mappingRationale: Backdoor/Trapdoor implies supply chain or insider insertion (#10).

mappings.cweName: Improper Control of Dynamically-Managed Code Resources
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client -> Malware
mappings.mappingRationale: Implementation flaw allowing attacker influence over dynamically-managed code (eval, reflection, dynamic class loading). Server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) per R-ROLE. Per R-EXEC, dynamic code resources execute attacker-influenced code — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Control of Dynamically-Identified Variables
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper control of dynamically-identified variables (PHP variable variables, JS object[name] with attacker-controlled name) — attacker selects which variable is read/written. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
mappings.mappingRationale: Mass assignment — server-side framework auto-binds request fields to model attributes (Rails, Django, Spring) without an allowlist, letting attackers set fields they should not control. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
mappings.mappingRationale: Fast-but-insecure password hashing (MD5/SHA1) lets attackers brute-force credentials offline, enabling impersonation. Per ruling-2 → #4.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement ('Expression Language Injection')
mappings.mappingRationale: Server-side sanitization flaw allowing attacker input to be evaluated by an expression-language engine (Spring SpEL, Struts OGNL, JSP EL). Per R-EXEC, EL evaluation of attacker-controlled input executes foreign code — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
mappings.mappingRationale: Server fetches a URL whose target is attacker-controlled, letting the attacker reach internal endpoints (cloud metadata, internal services) from the server's network position. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (abuse of the fetch function).

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Power Consumption
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — missing power-consumption restriction — battery drain on mobile/IoT devices. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Storage of Sensitive Data in a Mechanism without Access Control
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive data stored in a mechanism that lacks access control (world-readable file, unprotected shared memory, public Android intent extra). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive data stored without proper access protection (file/dir/registry permissions, missing encryption-at-rest). Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (the storage function is configured to admit the wrong callers).

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
mappings.mappingRationale: Failure to verify the intended endpoint of a communication channel lets an attacker substitute a controlled endpoint. Decision tree Q9 -> #1 (channel-spoofing via the connection-establishment function).

mappings.cweName: Improper Enforcement of Message Integrity During Transmission in a Communication Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Failure to verify message integrity in transit — attacker on the wire can modify content undetected. Decision tree Q4 -> #5.

mappings.cweName: Improper Verification of Intent by Broadcast Receiver
mappings.mappingRationale: Android broadcast receiver does not verify the intent's sender/action, letting any app invoke the receiver. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Export of Android Application Components
mappings.mappingRationale: Android component (Activity, Service, Receiver) is exported without proper permission protection, lettable any app invoke it. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Use of Implicit Intent for Sensitive Communication
mappings.mappingRationale: Implicit Android intent for sensitive communication can be received by any matching app, including a malicious one. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Authorization in Handler for Custom URL Scheme
mappings.mappingRationale: Custom URL scheme handler does not authorize the caller, letting any web origin invoke its functions via the registered scheme. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing/insufficient verification that a received message originated from the expected source — spoofing/relay possible. Decision tree Q4 -> #5.

mappings.cweName: Incorrectly Specified Destination in a Communication Channel
mappings.mappingRationale: Communication is sent to an incorrectly-specified destination (wrong host, wrong port, wrong topic), letting attacker-controlled endpoints receive the data. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
mappings.mappingRationale: Cross-domain policy (Flash crossdomain.xml, Silverlight clientaccesspolicy.xml) lists overly broad domains, letting untrusted origins access cross-origin resources. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
mappings.mappingRationale: Data-query-language injection (NoSQL, XQuery, OQL, ORM-DSL) — attacker payload modifies the query semantics. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Research Concepts
mappings.mappingRationale: Organizational view (CWE-1000 Research Concepts view), not a concrete weakness. Per R-Q0, view nodes are Prohibited.

mappings.cweName: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing HttpOnly exposes the session cookie to JavaScript-readable storage; the dominant downstream threat is cookie theft for impersonation. Decision tree Q3 → #4. The XSS cluster (#3) is a separate acquisition vector per R-CRED.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Visual Distinction of Homoglyphs Presented to User
mappings.mappingRationale: This weakness facilitates deception and phishing attacks (#9) by making malicious identifiers look legitimate.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames
mappings.mappingRationale: This vulnerability (Clickjacking) is primarily used to trick the user (#9) into performing actions they did not intend.

mappings.cweName: Use of Web Link to Untrusted Target with window.opener Access
mappings.mappingRationale: Allows a target site to redirect the referring page (Reverse Tabnabbing), mainly used for phishing (#9).

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Comparison with Missing Factors
mappings.mappingRationale: Comparison missing necessary factors (e.g., comparing username only when tenant must also match). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Comparison of Incompatible Types
mappings.mappingRationale: Comparison of incompatible types yields unexpected coerced result. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Comparison Using Wrong Factors
mappings.mappingRationale: Comparison uses wrong factors (e.g., reference equality when content equality intended). Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Processor Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Compiler/processor optimization removes security-relevant code (e.g., explicit memset of sensitive buffer optimized away because the buffer is dead). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Insecure Automated Optimizations
mappings.mappingRationale: Insecure automated optimization introduced by tooling (compiler, transpiler, minifier) silently changes program semantics in security-relevant ways. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Inadequate Detection or Handling of Adversarial Input Perturbations in Automated Recognition Mechanism
mappings.mappingRationale: Adversarial-input attacks (data poisoning, evasion) abuse the model's intended inference function by crafting inputs the model processes correctly but the user's downstream logic interprets unsafely. Per Axiom IV (actor identity does not determine cluster), this is #1 regardless of whether the adversary is a user, attacker, or insider.

mappings.cweName: Use of Redundant Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (redundant code). Per the verdict policy, code-quality patterns are Discouraged (no defensible threat cluster), not Prohibited (which is reserved for Category/View/Deprecated nodes).

mappings.cweName: Static Member Data Element outside of a Singleton Class Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (static member outside singleton). Non-threat code pattern.

mappings.cweName: Data Element Aggregating an Excessively Large Number of Non-Primitive Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (data element with too many fields). Non-threat code pattern.

mappings.cweName: Architecture with Number of Horizontal Layers Outside of Expected Range
mappings.mappingRationale: Architecture-quality issue (excessive horizontal layers). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Parent Class with a Virtual Destructor and a Child Class without a Virtual Destructor
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (parent virtual destructor with non-virtual child). Non-threat unless it causes specific memory-safety bug, classified at that level.

mappings.cweName: Creation of Immutable Text Using String Concatenation
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/performance issue (string concatenation for immutables). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Modules with Circular Dependencies
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (circular module dependencies). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Invokable Control Element with Large Number of Outward Calls
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (control element with too many outward calls). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Data Query Operations in a Large Data Table
mappings.mappingRationale: Performance issue that can be abused for Resource Exhaustion (#6).

mappings.cweName: Excessive Platform Resource Consumption within a Loop
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — excessive platform-resource consumption inside a loop — amplifies cost per iteration. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Initialization with Hard-Coded Network Resource Configuration Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Hard-coded network endpoint (server URL, registry hostname) creates a fixed function the attacker can spoof or redirect by controlling the named resource (DNS hijack, BGP attack). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Use of Hard-Coded Literals in Initialization
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (excessive hard-coded literals). Specific security-relevant cases classify at child CWE-547 (now also Discouraged).

mappings.cweName: Missing Documentation for Design
mappings.mappingRationale: Documentation gap (missing design documentation). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Invocation of a Control Element at an Unnecessarily Deep Horizontal Layer
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (control element invoked at unnecessarily deep nesting / call-stack level). Non-threat maintainability concern with no defensible threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: Multiple Inheritance from Concrete Classes
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (multiple inheritance from concrete classes). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Invokable Control Element with Variadic Parameters
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (variadic parameters complicating validation). Specific validation defects classify at child CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Data Access Operations Outside of Expected Data Manager Component
mappings.mappingRationale: Architecture issue (data access outside data-manager component). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Invokable Control Element in Multi-Thread Context with non-Final Static Storable or Member Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Invokable control element used in multi-thread context without thread safety. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Technical Documentation
mappings.mappingRationale: Documentation gap (insufficient technical documentation). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Number of Inefficient Server-Side Data Accesses
mappings.mappingRationale: Performance defect (excessive server-side data accesses in a loop). Hypothetical link to #6 DoS is too weak to defend a cluster mapping; specific exploitable cases classify at child CWE-407 (algorithmic complexity).

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Encapsulation
mappings.mappingRationale: Design principle violation. Specific exploitable consequences (e.g., public mutable state) are captured by child CWEs (CWE-493, 500, 582, 766). Classify at the child level.

mappings.cweName: Parent Class with References to Child Class
mappings.mappingRationale: Design issue (parent class referencing child class). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Creation of Class Instance within a Static Code Block
mappings.mappingRationale: Performance/design issue (instance creation in static block). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Invokable Control Element with Signature Containing an Excessive Number of Parameters
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (signature with excessive parameters). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Runtime Resource Management Control Element in a Component Built to Run on Application Servers
mappings.mappingRationale: Reliability/best-practice issue (runtime resource management in unexpected component). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Missing Serialization Control Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing serialization control element on a class that should be serializable, leading to deserialization-handling defects in code that round-trips the data. Code implementation flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Execution of Sequential Searches of Data Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Algorithmic complexity/Performance issue leading to DoS (LoA).

mappings.cweName: Inconsistency Between Implementation and Documented Design
mappings.mappingRationale: Documentation/implementation drift. Non-threat by itself; specific drift consequences classify at child CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Empty Exception Block
mappings.mappingRationale: Error-handling code-quality issue (empty exception block). Specific exploitable consequences classify at the child level.

mappings.cweName: Serializable Data Element Containing non-Serializable Item Elements
mappings.mappingRationale: Reliability issue (non-serializable item in serializable element). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Empty Code Block
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (empty code block — possibly missing logic, possibly intentional placeholder). Non-threat unless the missing logic was a security check, in which case classify the specific missing control.

mappings.cweName: Data Resource Access without Use of Connection Pooling
mappings.mappingRationale: Performance defect (data access without connection pooling). Reliability/scalability issue, not a threat cluster. Specific DoS-via-resource-exhaustion cases classify at child CWE-770/774.

mappings.cweName: Non-SQL Invokable Control Element with Excessive Number of Data Resource Accesses
mappings.mappingRationale: Performance defect (non-SQL invokable element with too many data accesses). Reliability issue, not a threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: Class with Excessively Deep Inheritance
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (excessively deep inheritance). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Unconditional Control Flow Transfer outside of Switch Block
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability/control-flow issue. Non-threat unless it causes a specific exploitable defect.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Adherence to Expected Conventions
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (insufficient adherence to conventions). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Floating Point Comparison with Incorrect Operator
mappings.mappingRationale: Floating-point comparison using == when an epsilon-tolerance is required. Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Inappropriate Source Code Style or Formatting
mappings.mappingRationale: Source-code style issue (inappropriate formatting). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Parent Class without Virtual Destructor Method
mappings.mappingRationale: Parent class without virtual destructor — derived class destruction skips parent cleanup, leaking resources or leaving partially-destroyed state. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Source Code File with Excessive Number of Lines of Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (file with too many lines). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Class Instance Self Destruction Control Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Class instance self-destruction is a reliability/lifecycle defect; absent a specific exploitable consequence (UAF, double-free), it does not classify to a threat cluster. Specific exploitable cases classify at child CWEs (CWE-415, 416).

mappings.cweName: Data Access from Outside Expected Data Manager Component
mappings.mappingRationale: Architecture violation (data access outside expected manager). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Invokable Control Element with Excessive File or Data Access Operations
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (control element with excessive file/data access). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Invokable Control Element with Excessive Volume of Commented-out Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (excessive comment volume). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Class with Excessive Number of Child Classes
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (class with too many children). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Class with Virtual Method without a Virtual Destructor
mappings.mappingRationale: Class with virtual methods but no virtual destructor — same hazard as CWE-1079 in C++. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Synchronous Access of Remote Resource without Timeout
mappings.mappingRationale: Synchronous remote-resource access without timeout — caller hangs indefinitely on misbehaving server, leading to thread exhaustion and DoS. Error-handling code implementation flaw — failure to detect/propagate the condition leaves the program in an undefined or insecure state. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Large Data Table with Excessive Number of Indices
mappings.mappingRationale: Performance issue leading to potential Resource Exhaustion (#6).

mappings.cweName: Method Containing Access of a Member Element from Another Class
mappings.mappingRationale: Encapsulation issue (member access from another object). Non-threat unless leveraged for state corruption, classified at the specific defect.

mappings.cweName: Use of Object without Invoking Destructor Method
mappings.mappingRationale: Object used without invoking its destructor — resource leak. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Same Invokable Control Element in Multiple Architectural Layers
mappings.mappingRationale: Architecture issue (same control element in multiple components). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessively Complex Data Representation
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability defect — data representation complexity hinders correct handling but does not itself classify to a threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Index Range Scan for a Data Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Performance defect (excessive index-range scan). Hypothetical link to #6 is too weak; specific DoS cases classify at child CWE-407.

mappings.cweName: Loop Condition Value Update within the Loop
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (loop condition updated within loop). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Singleton Class Instance Creation without Proper Locking or Synchronization
mappings.mappingRationale: Singleton creation without proper locking permits multiple instances or partially-initialized state. Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Persistent Storable Data Element without Associated Comparison Control Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Persistent storable data lacking the comparison element required for proper change detection / equality. Code implementation flaw -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Data Element containing Pointer Item without Proper Copy Control Element
mappings.mappingRationale: Pointer-containing data element copied without proper deep-copy — aliasing creates UAF / double-free. Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Inconsistent Naming Conventions for Identifiers
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (inconsistent identifier names). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Isolation of System-Dependent Functions
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality/portability issue (insufficient isolation of system-dependent functions). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Runtime Component in Generated Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Generated code relies on a runtime component that may be missing, mismatched, or substituted, exposing the deployment to supply-chain risk. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Machine-Dependent Data Representation
mappings.mappingRationale: Portability issue (machine-dependent data representation). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Use of Platform-Dependent Third Party Components
mappings.mappingRationale: Portability issue (platform-dependent third-party components). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of unmaintained third-party components — known-but-unfixed vulnerabilities accumulate; trust-acceptance event is the import. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Encapsulation of Machine-Dependent Functionality
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (insufficient encapsulation of machine-dependent functionality). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Use of Symbolic Constants
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (insufficient symbolic constants — magic numbers). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Isolation of Symbolic Constant Definitions
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (insufficient isolation of constant definitions). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Reliance on Global Variables
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (excessive globals). Non-threat unless leveraged for state corruption, classified at the specific defect.

mappings.cweName: Use of Same Variable for Multiple Purposes
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (variable used for multiple purposes). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Design Documentation
mappings.mappingRationale: Documentation gap (incomplete design documentation). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete I/O Documentation
mappings.mappingRationale: Documentation gap (incomplete I/O documentation). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Incomplete Documentation of Program Execution

mappings.mappingRationale: Source-code style issue (inappropriate comment style). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Inappropriate Whitespace Style
mappings.mappingRationale: Source-code style issue (inappropriate whitespace style). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Source Code Element without Standard Prologue
mappings.mappingRationale: Source-code style issue (missing standard prologue). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Inaccurate Comments
mappings.mappingRationale: Documentation/quality issue (inaccurate comments). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Callable with Insufficient Behavioral Summary
mappings.mappingRationale: Documentation/quality issue (callable with insufficient behavioral summary). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Documentation of Error Handling Techniques
mappings.mappingRationale: Documentation gap (insufficient documentation of error-handling). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Use of Unconditional Branching
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (excessive unconditional branching). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Code Complexity
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability defect — complexity makes correctness review harder but does not itself classify to a threat cluster.

mappings.cweName: Excessive McCabe Cyclomatic Complexity
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (excessive McCabe cyclomatic complexity). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Halstead Complexity
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (excessive Halstead complexity). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Use of Self-Modifying Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (self-modifying code). Non-threat unless used as anti-debug malware technique, in which case classify at the specific weakness.

mappings.cweName: Excessively Deep Nesting
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability issue (excessive nesting depth). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Excessive Attack Surface
mappings.mappingRationale: Meta-property of a system, not a concrete weakness — every cluster could contribute. Classify at the specific exposed function/CWE instead.

mappings.cweName: Declaration of Variable with Unnecessarily Wide Scope
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality issue (variable scope wider than necessary). Non-threat.

mappings.cweName: Compilation with Insufficient Warnings or Errors
mappings.mappingRationale: Build-process issue (insufficient compiler warnings). Non-threat by itself; defects it would have caught classify at their specific CWE.

mappings.cweName: Irrelevant Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Code-quality defect (dead/unused code). Not itself a threat action; if it gets reachable later, classify at that point by the actual exposed weakness.

mappings.cweName: Improper Use of Validation Framework
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper use of a validation framework (skipping the framework, configuring it incorrectly) lets unfiltered input reach the consumer. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: ASP.NET Misconfiguration: Improper Model Validation
mappings.mappingRationale: ASP.NET model-validation framework misconfigured — server-side request inputs reach business logic without validation. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Inefficient CPU Computation
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — inefficient CPU computation — algorithmic complexity not appropriate for input size. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Use of Prohibited Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Too generic — the cluster depends entirely on what the prohibited code does. Classify at the specific weakness the prohibited code introduces.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Use of Uninitialized Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A. Rolled into CWE-908 (Use of Uninitialized Resource).

mappings.cweName: Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource initialized with an insecure default (public, weak permission, debug-on) that the deployer must remember to harden. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Improper Isolation of Shared Resources on System-on-a-Chip (SoC)
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware-level implementation flaw (SoC) often reachable via physical/side-channel or low-level exploit.

mappings.cweName: DMA Device Enabled Too Early in Boot Phase
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — DMA controller activated before access-control configuration completes, allowing unrestricted memory read during boot. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: On-Chip Debug and Test Interface With Improper Access Control
mappings.mappingRationale: JTAG/Debug interfaces are typically physical access vectors.

mappings.cweName: Improper Identifier for IP Block used in System-On-Chip (SOC)
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — incorrect identifier for an IP block in the SoC interconnect — security policy applied to the wrong block. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Power-On of Untrusted Execution Core Before Enabling Fabric Access Control
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — untrusted execution core powered on before fabric access control engaged, allowing initial code execution to bypass restrictions. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Hardware Design
mappings.mappingRationale: Organizational view (CWE-1194 Hardware Design view), not a concrete weakness. Children typically map to #8 Physical Attack or #10 Supply Chain Attack — classify at the child level. Per R-Q0, view nodes are Prohibited.

mappings.cweName: Generation of Weak Initialization Vector (IV)
mappings.mappingRationale: Weak/predictable IVs degrade encryption confidentiality, recoverable by an interceptor. Per ruling-2 → #5.

mappings.cweName: Failure to Disable Reserved Bits
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — reserved (debug/test) bits not disabled in production silicon. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
mappings.mappingRationale: Access control granularity is too coarse (one privilege covers many actions), letting holders abuse capabilities they did not need. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Register Defaults or Module Parameters
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — register defaults / module parameters set to insecure values at reset. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Granularity of Address Regions Protected by Register Locks
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — address-region protection too coarse — an unintended adjacent region is covered or excluded. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Race Condition for Write-Once Attributes
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — race condition for write-once attributes — two writers compete for the one allowed write. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Write-Once Bit Fields
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — write-once bit fields can actually be modified after first write. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Creation of Emergent Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Abstract concept describing how unanticipated resources arise; the exploitable cluster depends on what the emergent resource is and how it is exposed. Classify at the concrete child weakness.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information Through Metadata
mappings.mappingRationale: Sensitive information leaked via metadata (EXIF, document properties, version-control metadata embedded in releases). Implementation flaw in the content-generation function. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Prevention of Lock Bit Modification
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — lock-bit modification not properly prevented after asserted, defeating immutability guarantees. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Lock Behavior After Power State Transition
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — lock state not preserved across power-state transitions, resetting protection at sleep/wake. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Security-Sensitive Hardware Controls with Missing Lock Bit Protection
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — security-sensitive controls have no lock bit, leaving them mutable indefinitely. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Hardware Internal or Debug Modes Allow Override of Locks
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware debug-interface flaw — internal debug modes can override lock-bit protections. Debug paths typically require physical or local access. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Use of Autoboxing and Unboxing for Performance Critical Operations
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — unintended autoboxing/unboxing in hot loops — performance collapse exploitable for DoS. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
mappings.mappingRationale: CSV Injection attacks the client spreadsheet application (#3).

mappings.cweName: Improper Zeroization of Hardware Register
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware data-remanence flaw — hardware register not zeroized between contexts, leaking previous state. Physical access can recover residual data. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Use of a Cryptographic Primitive with a Risky Implementation
mappings.mappingRationale: A flawed primitive implementation (e.g., side-channel-leaking AES, broken curve params) degrades the protection of encrypted data, recoverable by an attacker. Per ruling-2 → #5.

mappings.cweName: Use of Predictable Algorithm in Random Number Generator
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Identity Theft or Man in the Middle
mappings.mappingRationale: Predictable algorithm in an RNG produces guessable outputs. Token/identifier use -> #4 (impersonation); key/IV use -> #5 (channel decryption). Per ruling-2; consistent with CWE-331-339 PRNG family.

mappings.cweName: Inclusion of Undocumented Features or Chicken Bits
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — undocumented features / chicken bits left enabled in shipped silicon — supply-chain-style backdoor. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Sensitive Non-Volatile Information Not Protected During Debug
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware debug-interface flaw — sensitive non-volatile data not protected during debug-mode access. Debug paths typically require physical or local access. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Internal Asset Exposed to Unsafe Debug Access Level or State
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware debug-interface flaw — internal asset reachable from debug interface despite policy. Debug paths typically require physical or local access. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Finite State Machines (FSMs) in Hardware Logic
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — finite state machine has unintended/missing transitions reachable through input glitches. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Write Handling in Limited-write Non-Volatile Memories
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — limited-write non-volatile memory worn out by attacker writes — reliability/DoS. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Protection Against Voltage and Clock Glitches
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware fault-injection vulnerability — missing protection against voltage / clock glitching — fault injection induces instruction skipping or signal misinterpretation. Physical perturbation of the chip drives unintended state. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Semiconductor Defects in Hardware Logic with Security-Sensitive Implications
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — semiconductor defects exploitable via physical access (probing, fault injection). Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Application-Level Admin Tool with Inconsistent View of Underlying Operating System
mappings.mappingRationale: Per Axiom III a consequence (state inconsistency) of other attacks, not a generic vulnerability cause.

mappings.cweName: Improper Preservation of Consistency Between Independent Representations of Shared State
mappings.mappingRationale: Abstract logic-flaw umbrella. Specific consistency-violation defects classify at child CWEs.

mappings.cweName: Mirrored Regions with Different Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — mirrored memory regions hold different values, creating policy-vs-content discrepancy. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: CPU Hardware Not Configured to Support Exclusivity of Write and Execute Operations
mappings.mappingRationale: Missing W^X/DEP/NX enforcement makes injected shellcode directly executable, amplifying memory-corruption exploits in server-role (#2) or client-role (#3) code per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Selection of Fuse Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — incorrect fuse value selected at manufacturing, leaving security feature disabled. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Comparison Logic Granularity
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — comparison logic granularity too coarse / too fine for the security identifiers being compared. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Comparison Logic is Vulnerable to Power Side-Channel Attacks
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware side-channel — comparison logic leaks via power side-channel (differential power analysis). Information leaks via physical/microarchitectural observation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Software Interfaces to Hardware Features
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Abuse of Functions or Physical Attack
mappings.mappingRationale: Software-exposed interfaces to hardware features (debug, JTAG, register access). Software-vector exploitation abuses the exposed function (#1); physical-vector exploitation requires hardware access (#8). Context determines which.

mappings.cweName: Improper Access Control Applied to Mirrored or Aliased Memory Regions
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — mirrored / aliased memory not covered by the same access-control policy as the primary range. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive System Information Due to Uncleared Debug Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware debug-interface flaw — sensitive system info exposed because debug state was not cleared on entering production mode. Debug paths typically require physical or local access. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Security Token Assignment
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — security-token assignment policy in the SoC permits unintended principals to claim sensitive tokens. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Overlap Between Protected Memory Ranges
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — overlap between protected memory ranges produces ambiguity in which policy applies. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Single Event Upsets
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware fault-injection vulnerability — single-event upsets (cosmic rays, EM glitches) flip security-relevant bits. Physical perturbation of the chip drives unintended state. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Access Control for Register Interface
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — register interface lacks access control — any caller can read/write security-sensitive registers. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Physical Access Control
mappings.mappingRationale: Direct physical-access-control flaw — physical security boundary (lock, enclosure, port cover) missing or insufficient. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Hardware Logic with Insecure De-Synchronization between Control and Data Channels
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — hardware logic with insecure de-synchronization between clock domains — Meltdown-class transient-execution behavior. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Unintended Reentrant Invocation of Non-reentrant Code Via Nested Calls
mappings.mappingRationale: Unintended reentrant invocation of non-reentrant code (e.g., signal handler reentering malloc). Concurrency/race-condition code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Scrubbing of Sensitive Data from Decommissioned Device
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware data-remanence flaw — decommissioned device retains sensitive data because scrubbing is incomplete or skipped. Physical access can recover residual data. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Policy Uses Obsolete Encoding
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — security policy uses obsolete encoding that can no longer encode current actor identifiers, falling back to permissive defaults. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Policy Privileges are not Assigned Consistently Between Control and Data Agents
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — SoC policy privileges assigned inconsistently between IP blocks, creating asymmetric protection. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Product Released in Non-Release Configuration
mappings.mappingRationale: Product shipped in non-release configuration (debug enabled, test endpoints reachable, default credentials active). Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Generation of Incorrect Security Tokens
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — incorrect security tokens generated by hardware logic, miscategorizing principals. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Uninitialized Value on Reset for Registers Holding Security Settings
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — registers holding security settings not initialized to known value on reset. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Sensitive Information Uncleared Before Debug/Power State Transition
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — sensitive information not cleared before transitioning to debug/power state where new principals can observe. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Device Unlock Credential Sharing
mappings.mappingRationale: Device unlock credentials are shared across many devices (master key) — once leaked, every device is unlockable. Supply-chain key-management flaw. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: Improper Access Control for Volatile Memory Containing Boot Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — volatile memory holding boot code lacks access control — Secure Boot bypass. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute
mappings.mappingRationale: SameSite attribute not set to Lax/Strict on a sensitive cookie, leaving the cookie attached to cross-site requests and enabling CSRF (#1).

mappings.cweName: Hardware Child Block Incorrectly Connected to Parent System
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — hardware child block incorrectly connected to parent, routing data outside intended path. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Firmware Not Updateable
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability defect — non-updateable firmware prevents remediation but does not itself constitute a threat action against any single cluster.

mappings.cweName: Missing Protection Against Hardware Reverse Engineering Using Integrated Circuit (IC) Imaging Techniques
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — missing anti-tamper / anti-reverse-engineering protections on shipped silicon. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Cryptographic Operations are run Before Supporting Units are Ready
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — cryptographic operations executed before supporting hardware (entropy source, key registers) is fully initialized. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Access Control Check Implemented After Asset is Accessed
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — access-control check implemented after the asset is already accessed — TOCTOU at the hardware layer. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Sequence of Processor Instructions Leads to Unexpected Behavior
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — specific instruction sequences cause unexpected microarchitectural behavior (Spectre/Meltdown gadget classes). Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Assumed-Immutable Data is Stored in Writable Memory
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — data assumed immutable is stored in writable memory — Secure Boot / attestation bypass. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Mutable Attestation or Measurement Reporting Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — attestation/measurement reporting data is mutable — Secure Boot / TPM-style attestation defeated. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input
mappings.mappingRationale: Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input
mappings.mappingRationale: Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Syntactic Correctness of Input
mappings.mappingRationale: Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input
mappings.mappingRationale: Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Consistency within Input
mappings.mappingRationale: Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input
mappings.mappingRationale: Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Decoding of Security Identifiers
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — incorrect decoding of security identifiers — wrong principal authenticated. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Public Key Re-Use for Signing both Debug and Production Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Same public key trusted for both debug and production signing — debug signing capability authenticates production-grade artifacts. Supply-chain key-management flaw. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Conversion of Security Identifiers
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — incorrect conversion between security-identifier representations — privilege confusion. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Missing Source Correlation of Multiple Independent Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Security decision relies on a single data source without correlating against independent sources; spoofing one source defeats the check. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insecure Security Identifier Mechanism
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — insecure security-identifier mechanism (predictable, low-entropy, mutable). Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Debug Messages Revealing Unnecessary Information
mappings.mappingRationale: Debug messages reveal unnecessary information (stack traces, paths, internal state) to users. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Chaining or Granularity of Debug Components
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware debug-interface flaw — incorrect chaining or granularity of debug components — wider debug visibility than intended. Debug paths typically require physical or local access. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Unprotected Confidential Information on Device is Accessible by OSAT Vendors
mappings.mappingRationale: Confidential information left unprotected on the device after manufacturing/supply-chain stages. Decision tree Q8 -> #10 (supply-chain handoff event).

mappings.cweName: Hardware Logic Contains Race Conditions
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — hardware logic contains race conditions exploitable via timing. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Missing Protection Mechanism for Alternate Hardware Interface
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — missing protection mechanism for an alternate hardware path that bypasses the primary protection. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Protection of Physical Side Channels
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware side-channel — missing/insufficient protection against physical side channels (power, EM, acoustic). Information leaks via physical/microarchitectural observation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient or Incomplete Data Removal within Hardware Component
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware data-remanence flaw — insufficient/incomplete data removal within hardware (cache lines, register files retain residue). Physical access can recover residual data. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Missing Source Identifier in Entity Transactions on a System-On-Chip (SOC)
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — missing source identifier in fabric transactions — receiver cannot tell who issued the command. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Non-Transparent Sharing of Microarchitectural Resources
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware side-channel — non-transparent sharing of microarchitectural resources (Meltdown/Spectre/MDS class). Information leaks via physical/microarchitectural observation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improperly Preserved Integrity of Hardware Configuration State During a Power Save/Restore Operation
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — hardware configuration integrity not preserved across state transitions (reset, sleep). Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Logic in Memory Address Decoding
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware logic flaw exploitable via physical effects (e.g., Rowhammer). Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer weakness) → #8.

mappings.cweName: Missing Ability to Patch ROM Code
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability defect — non-patchable ROM prevents remediation of any future weakness but does not itself classify to a cluster.

mappings.cweName: Improper Translation of Security Attributes by Fabric Bridge
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — security attributes mistranslated by fabric bridge between protocol domains. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Missing Protection for Mirrored Regions in On-Chip Fabric Firewall
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — mirrored regions in on-chip memory lack protection that primary region has. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Hardware Allows Activation of Test or Debug Logic at Runtime
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware debug-interface flaw — hardware permits activation of test/debug logic in production silicon. Debug paths typically require physical or local access. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Missing Write Protection for Parametric Data Values
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — parametric data values (clock dividers, voltage settings) lack write protection — manipulable to cause faults. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Setting of Bus Controlling Capability in Fabric End-point
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — bus-controlling capability assigned incorrectly in fabric end-node configuration. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Fabric-Address Map Allows Programming of Unwarranted Overlaps of Protected and Unprotected Ranges
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — fabric-address map permits programming of unwarranted/overlapping ranges. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Access Control in Fabric Bridge
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — fabric bridge lacks proper access control between protocol domains. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Missing Support for Security Features in On-chip Fabrics or Buses
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — on-chip fabric lacks support for security features needed by upstream blocks. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Protection against Electromagnetic Fault Injection (EM-FI)
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware fault-injection vulnerability — missing protection against electromagnetic fault injection. Physical perturbation of the chip drives unintended state. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Protection for Outbound Error Messages and Alert Signals
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware protection/access-control flaw — outbound error messages and altered branch behavior insufficiently protected — leak via observation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
mappings.mappingRationale: Prototype pollution — attacker mutates Object prototype, affecting downstream type checks and access patterns. Code implementation flaw in property-assignment logic. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 (Node.js) or client-role #3 (browser JS) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Use of Blocking Code in Single-threaded, Non-blocking Context
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of blocking code in single-threaded non-blocking context (Node.js, browser main thread) — long synchronous operations stall the event loop, causing DoS. Code implementation flaw -> server-role #2 (Node) or client-role #3 (browser) per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Management of Sensitive Trace Data
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware debug-interface flaw — sensitive trace data managed insecurely — exposed via debug interfaces. Debug paths typically require physical or local access. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: DEPRECATED: Sensitive Information Accessible by Physical Probing of JTAG Interface
mappings.mappingRationale: Deprecated CWE entry. Per the verdict policy, deprecated entries are Prohibited and map to N/A.

mappings.cweName: Improperly Controlled Sequential Memory Allocation
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource exhaustion / denial of service — improperly-controlled sequential memory allocation — allocation count grows unboundedly with input. Decision tree Q5 (resource exhaustion / capacity weakness) -> #6.

mappings.cweName: Missing Immutable Root of Trust in Hardware
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — missing immutable root of trust in hardware — boot integrity cannot be anchored. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address
mappings.mappingRationale: Service binds to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces) instead of a restricted interface, exposing functions intended for local use to the network. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Security Version Number Mutable to Older Versions
mappings.mappingRationale: Security version number can be downgraded — attacker reverts to an older, vulnerable version that still passes signature checks. Decision tree Q8 -> #10 (downgrade as a supply-chain trust-acceptance attack).

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Component That is Not Updateable
mappings.mappingRationale: Maintainability defect — relying on a non-updateable component prevents remediation of latent weaknesses but does not itself classify to a cluster.

mappings.cweName: Remanent Data Readable after Memory Erase
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware data-remanence flaw — remanent data readable after memory erase (cell-level retention beyond explicit clear). Physical access can recover residual data. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Isolation of Shared Resources in Network On Chip (NoC)
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — shared resources in network-on-chip not properly isolated between IP blocks. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Faults that Lead to Instruction Skips
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware fault-injection vulnerability — faults that lead to instruction skipping not properly handled — fault injection bypasses checks. Physical perturbation of the chip drives unintended state. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
mappings.mappingRationale: Inefficient regex enables ReDoS — one crafted input triggers exponential backtracking. Code defect (the regex pattern) -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Unauthorized Error Injection Can Degrade Hardware Redundancy
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware fault-injection vulnerability — unauthorized error injection can degrade hardware function — controlled stress-induced misbehavior. Physical perturbation of the chip drives unintended state. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Bitwise Shift of Integer
mappings.mappingRationale: Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
mappings.tlctcMappingName: Exploiting Server -> Malware OR Exploiting Client -> Malware
mappings.mappingRationale: Sanitization flaw allowing attacker input to be evaluated by a template engine. Server-Side Template Injection (#2, e.g., Jinja2/Velocity) or Client-Side Template Injection (#3, e.g., AngularJS) per R-ROLE. Per R-EXEC, template-engine evaluation executes attacker code — append → #7.

mappings.cweName: Improper Protections Against Hardware Overheating
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware overheating-protection flaw — controlled thermal stress causes physical damage or operational degradation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Insufficient Precision or Accuracy of a Real Number
mappings.mappingRationale: Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Multiple Releases of Same Resource or Handle
mappings.mappingRationale: Multiple releases of the same resource/handle (double free, double close). Memory-safety code implementation flaw. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Information Exposure through Microarchitectural State after Transient Execution
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware side-channel — information leak through microarchitectural state remaining after transient (speculative) execution — Spectre/Meltdown family. Information leaks via physical/microarchitectural observation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Hardware Behavior in Exceptionally Cold Environments
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware misbehaves under exceptional physical/environmental conditions (extreme temperature, voltage, EMI) — fault-injection vector. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on Insufficiently Trustworthy Component
mappings.mappingRationale: Reliance on a third-party component whose trustworthiness is insufficient (untracked provenance, abandonware, suspicious supply chain). Trust-acceptance event when the component is imported. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: Improper Handling of Physical or Environmental Conditions
mappings.mappingRationale: Improper handling of physical/environmental conditions creates exploitable state under controlled physical input. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Missing Origin Validation in WebSockets
mappings.mappingRationale: WebSocket handler does not validate the Origin header, enabling Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking. Decision tree Q9 -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Insecure Operation on Windows Junction / Mount Point
mappings.mappingRationale: Windows junction/mount-point manipulation lets an attacker redirect privileged file access to attacker-chosen locations. Path-traversal/equivalence variant — code implementation flaw in path canonicalization. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE. See CWE-22 for the parent class discussion.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Parsing of Numbers with Different Radices
mappings.mappingRationale: Numeric parsing accepts different radices (octal-leading-zero, 0x hex) inconsistently between security check and consumer, producing parsing-discrepancy bypass. Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Weak Authentication
mappings.mappingRationale: Authentication mechanism is weak by design (e.g., easily defeated challenge, missing replay protection). Per ruling-1, auth-LOGIC weakness -> #1.

mappings.cweName: Use of Weak Credentials
mappings.mappingRationale: The product uses weak credentials (e.g., default keys, hard-coded / easily guessable passwords) that an attacker can calculate, derive, reuse, or guess and then use to authenticate. In TLCTC this is #4 Identity Theft: the generic vulnerability is that the system accepts credentials that can be trivially created/guessed and used to impersonate a legitimate identity. No separate harvesting step (#3/#5/#7/#8) is implied by the CWE itself.

mappings.cweName: Use of Default Credentials
mappings.mappingRationale: Default credentials shipped with the product (passwords or cryptographic keys) — any attacker who knows the defaults can authenticate. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Use of Default Password
mappings.mappingRationale: The product uses default passwords for potentially critical functionality. Real-world exploits use these known passwords to bypass authentication and gain administrative/DBA access. This matches TLCTC #4 Identity Theft: the attacker possesses a known default password and uses it as a credential to operate under a legitimate identity. There is no requirement in the CWE text that the password be first harvested via another cluster, so it is not just an enabling condition.

mappings.cweName: Use of Default Cryptographic Key
mappings.mappingRationale: Default cryptographic key shipped with the product — once known, every deployment's protected operations can be impersonated. Decision tree Q3 -> #4.

mappings.cweName: Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component
mappings.mappingRationale: Dependency on a third-party component with known vulnerabilities — the trust-acceptance event imports the vulnerability into the product. Decision tree Q8 -> #10.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Initialization of Resource
mappings.mappingRationale: Resource initialized to an incorrect/unsafe value, propagating into security decisions. Input-validation code implementation flaw at the parser/validator boundary. Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information during Transient Execution
mappings.mappingRationale: Microarchitectural side-channel — sensitive information exposed during transient (speculative) execution via cache-state, branch predictor, or other shared microarchitectural structures. Spectre-class. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information in Shared Microarchitectural Structures during Transient Execution
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware side-channel — information leak through shared microarchitectural structures during transient execution. Information leaks via physical/microarchitectural observation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information caused by Incorrect Data Forwarding during Transient Execution
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware side-channel — information leak caused by incorrect data forwarding during transient execution. Information leaks via physical/microarchitectural observation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information caused by Shared Microarchitectural Predictor State that Influences Transient Execution
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware side-channel — information leak caused by shared microarchitectural predictor state influencing transient execution. Information leaks via physical/microarchitectural observation. Decision tree Q7 -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Incorrect Parsing of Numbers with Different Radices
mappings.mappingRationale: Numeric parsing accepts different radices (octal-leading-zero, 0x hex) inconsistently between security check and consumer, producing parsing-discrepancy bypass. Arithmetic/numeric code implementation flaw (overflow, underflow, sign issue, precision). Decision tree Q2 -> server-role #2 or client-role #3 per R-ROLE.

mappings.cweName: Improper Neutralization of Input Used for LLM Prompting
mappings.mappingRationale: Prompt injection — server-side LLM endpoint concatenates attacker input into the prompt, letting the attacker override system instructions. Decision tree Q2 -> #2.

mappings.cweName: Reliance on HTTP instead of HTTPS
mappings.mappingRationale: Use of HTTP where HTTPS is required leaves the channel exposed to interception, modification, and active downgrade. Decision tree Q4 -> #5.

mappings.cweName: Missing Security-Relevant Feedback for Unexecuted Operations in Hardware Interface
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — missing security-relevant feedback for unexecuted operations — caller cannot tell whether the operation actually completed. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.

mappings.cweName: Driving Intermediate Cryptographic State/Results to Hardware Module Outputs
mappings.mappingRationale: Hardware/SoC design flaw — intermediate cryptographic state/results driven onto observable buses — side-channel leak of in-progress crypto. Decision tree Q7 (physical-layer / hardware weakness) -> #8.
